# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alias, apache, approach (+104 more)

# Storyline Coverage Analytics in Monte Carlo Harness

## Problem Statement

The Monte Carlo balance harness (MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts) currently tracks card ownership, market offers, and economy history across simulation runs, but has no visibility into storyline event coverage. Storyline events — which form branching chains with accept/reject choices — are a key game mechanic, yet the harness cannot report how often storylines fire, how deeply their chains progress, whether cycles appear, or what impact storyline choices have on win rates. This leaves the balance team blind to storyline-related balance issues.

## Users

- **Balance team / game designers**: Want to understand whether storylines are contributing positively to the game (e.g., do "Accept" choices correlate with higher win rates? Do certain storylines trigger too or too rarely?).
- **Content designers**: Want to verify that all storylines are being exercised in simulation and that chains progress reasonably (not dead-ending too quickly or cycling excessively).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Storyline fire frequency**: The harness reports how many runs and what percentage feature each storyline (`storyline-economy`, `storyline-health`, `storyline-labor`, `storyline-restaurant`, `storyline-tax`), derived from event-choice transcript records captured during simulation runs.

2. **Chain depth tracking**: For each storyline event encountered, the harness tracks how far the chain progresses (number of consecutive chain cards pushed), reported per storyline as a distribution (mean, median, max depth) across runs.

3. **Cycle detection**: The harness detects and counts cycle occurrences (tax → tax-error → tax-inquiry → tax, per `storyline-manifest.json` edges with `cycle: true`), reporting cycle frequency per storyline and per run.

4. **Win-rate impact of choices**: For each storyline with choices (flu-outbreak, popular-menu, recession, strike-service, tax, tax-error, tax-inquiry), the harness computes the win-rate differential between "Accept" and "Reject" choices — similar to existing M2 win-rate delta pattern.

5. **Integration with existing analytics**: Storyline analytics are exposed as new functions in the balance engine (`src/scripts/balance/engine/`) following the same pattern as existing metrics (G1–G8, M1–M7), with graceful degradation when storyline data is absent.

## Constraints

- **Non-blocking**: This is a deferred enhancement; it must not change existing Monte Carlo harness behaviour (strategies, termination, output format for non-storyline fields).
- **Graceful degradation**: All new storyline metrics return `null` when event-choice data is not available in run summaries (consistent with existing M4/M6/G4/G6/G7 patterns).
- **Builds on existing transcript recording**: The harness already has a lazy `recordMainStreetEvent` call path via `require('./MainStreetTranscript')`; the extension should extend this path to capture event-choice data into a new field on `MonteCarloRunSummary`.
- **No UI changes required**: Output is analytical (JSON/CSV), consistent with existing harness output.

## Existing State

- Monte Carlo harness (`MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`) runs simulations with strategies (market-greedy, demo-greedy, greedy, banking-greedy, random) and records `MonteCarloRunSummary` per seed.
- The harness already records `cardsOwned`, `marketOffers`, and `economyHistory` on run summaries (Phase 1 data).
- Storyline events with choices are resolved in-engine; `recordStorylineResolution` in `MainStreetStoryline.ts` emits `event-choice` transcript events.
- The Monte Carlo harness has a try/catch wrapper for `recordMainStreetEvent` that silently ignores failures when no recorder is wired.
- Storyline manifest (`docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json`) defines 5 storylines, 14 edge transitions, and 1 cycle group.
- Balance engine (`src/scripts/balance/engine/`) has 8 global metrics (G1–G8) and 7 card metrics (M1–M7) with graceful degradation patterns.

## Desired Change

1. **Extend `MonteCarloRunSummary`** with a new field capturing event choices encountered during a run (event ID, choice made, chain depth at that point).
2. **Wire transcript recording** in the Monte Carlo harness so that event-choice events are captured (not just ai-action events).
3. **Add storyline analytics functions** to the balance engine:
   - `computeStorylineFireFrequency(runs)`: percentage of runs per storyline.
   - `computeChainDepthStats(runs)`: depth distribution per storyline.
   - `computeCycleStats(runs)`: cycle frequency per storyline and per run.
   - `computeChoiceWinRateDelta(runs, eventId)`: win-rate difference between Accept vs Reject.
4. **Export storyline metrics** from the balance engine barrel file.
5. **Add tests** covering all new analytics functions.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Extend `MonteCarloRunSummary` interface; wire transcript recording for event-choice events.
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/index.ts` — Barrel file for new storyline metrics exports.
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/storyline-metrics.ts` (new) — New analytics module for storyline-specific metrics.
- `tests/main-street/balance/storyline-metrics.test.ts` (new) — Tests for storyline analytics functions.
- `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` — Reference for storyline definitions and cycle edges (read-only).

## Related Work

- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** — write storylines (epic, completed): The parent epic that shipped the storyline system.
- **MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0** — Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema (completed): Provides the manifest data model.
- **MS-0MUMP96XH002SJ89** — Named storylines, outcome feedback & continuity indicator (completed): Provides storyline naming and feedback mechanics.
- **MS-0MUMP944B009PEO6** — Static validator & npm gate (completed): Validates storyline integrity.

Cross-repo change for core work item CG-0MUNC7FK5001T5CP (F7: Main Street first consumer).

Adds src/MainStreetAchievements.ts mapping the 12 CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES ids to persistent achievements via the engine-generic @core-engine/AchievementSystem, wired into the challenge completion callback in MainStreetChallenges.ts. No Steam SDK code in this repo; the sink resolves to the renderer IPC client in the Electron launcher and to a no-op elsewhere.

Updates the core submodule to a commit containing the achievement layer (F3) and renderer client (F6). Adds tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts (mapping completeness, launcher-manifest drift guard, idempotent unlock, sink delegation, completion-path wiring).

Core parent: CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `MainStreetAchievements.ts` declares an achievement manifest mapping all 12 `CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES` ids to achievement ids with titles, descriptions, and hidden flags; an automated test asserts every template is mapped exactly once.
- [ ] Challenge completion (including the mid-turn `evaluateChallengesAfterAction` path) unlocks the mapped achievement through the engine `AchievementSystem` exactly once per run, with no Steam SDK import anywhere in this repo.
- [ ] In the Electron launcher the unlock is forwarded over the F6 renderer client; in the browser and headless builds it uses the no-op or local sink and the game stays fully playable.
- [ ] Unit tests in the game repo cover mapping completeness, idempotent unlock, and sink delegation; they pass under `--project unit`.
- [ ] The mapping is validated against the launcher manifest (F4) so drift fails an automated check; the cross-repo change is committed and pushed to the game repo's `dev` branch only.

# Intake Brief: Serial Seller: achievement manifest entry + Steamworks API name

## Problem Statement

The new **Serial Seller** challenge (`ch-serial-seller`) must map to a persistent Steam achievement like the existing 12 challenges. The challenge-side mapping is added in the parent item (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J); this item covers the cross-repo pieces required before the parent can be reviewed.

## Users

- **Producers**: Need the Steam achievement registered on the Steamworks partner backend.
- **Developers**: Need the manifest entry to exist before the drift guard test will pass.
- **Players**: Need the Serial Seller achievement to appear in-game alongside the existing 12 achievements.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` contains a `serial-seller` entry with `steamApiName: TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` and `hidden: false`.
2. The Steamworks partner backend declares the matching `TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` achievement API name.
3. The `core` submodule pointer in the main-street repo is bumped to the commit containing the manifest change.
4. The manifest drift guard (`tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts`) passes with the parent's mapping in place.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The manifest lives in the `core` git submodule (a separate repository: `TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine`), requiring two repo operations.
- The `steamApiName` values must match exactly what is configured on the Steamworks partner backend, or Steam will silently drop the unlock.
- The achievement must not be hidden (`hidden: false`), consistent with the existing 12 challenges.
- The Steamworks backend configuration is a producer/external action that must be completed independently of code changes.

## Existing State

- 12 existing achievements in `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json`, all with the pattern `TCE_MAIN_STREET_<UPPER_SNAKE_CASE>`.
- The manifest is validated by `validateAchievementManifest()` and the drift guard test.
- Precedent: MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC (bumping core submodule pointer).

## Desired Change

- Add one entry to the manifest for the Serial Seller achievement.
- Commit to the core repo and bump the submodule pointer in main-street.
- Coordinate with the producer to register the achievement on Steamworks.

## Key Files (Predicted)

- `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` — Add `serial-seller` entry
- `core/` (git submodule) — Commit the manifest change
- `.gitmodules` / submodule index — Bump the submodule pointer

## Related Work

- **MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J**: Sell 3 businesses challenge (parent, blocked by this item)
- **MS-0MUNO0M2I004TK04**: Wire Main Street challenges to Steam achievements (parent epic)
- **MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC**: Precedent for bumping core submodule pointer

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Steamworks backend delay**: If the producer has not yet registered the achievement on Steamworks, the achievement will not unlock for players even after code changes land. This is tracked as a separate action.
- **Scope creep**: Additional achievement metadata (e.g., icons, descriptions) may be desired later; record as a follow-up, not in scope for this item.
- **Submodule conflict**: Unlikely but possible if the core repo has concurrent changes; resolve by rebasing on latest core before bumping.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

# Intake Brief: Track Synergy Diversity (G4/HHI) and Placement Dominance Post-Rebalance

## Problem Statement

Lower base incomes after the rebalance mean synergy bonuses represent a larger relative share of business income, making placement quality dominant over base economy. The synergy-diversity metric (G4/HHI) must be computed on the after-state Monte Carlo results to confirm no single synergy type is crowding out the others — a risk flagged in the rebalance intake.

## Users

- **Producer / Balance Team**: Needs a quantitative view of whether the rebalance created unintended synergy-type dominance that could narrow gameplay variety or create dominant strategy patterns.

## Existing State

- `computeSynergyDiversity()` already exists in `src/scripts/balance/engine/global-metrics.ts` — it computes the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI) of synergy type shares from `finalGrid` data on Monte Carlo run summaries.
- The function returns `{ hhi: number; synergyTypeShares: Record<string, number> }`.
- The function requires `finalGrid` (an array of card IDs representing the street grid at run end) on each run summary.
- `finalGrid` is **not currently captured** in `MonteCarloRunSummary` — the field is never populated.
- Card synergy types are defined per-card in `src/card-data.csv` (column `synergyTypes`), with 6 types: Food, Culture, Commerce, Service, Entertainment, Health.
- 10 of 39 business/community-space cards have multi-type synergy (e.g., 'Food|Culture'); the remaining 29 are single-type.
- The existing unit test (`global-metrics.test.ts`) uses a single `cardId → type` map, mapping each card to exactly one type.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **finalGrid is captured in Monte Carlo run summaries** — each `MonteCarloRunSummary` includes a `finalGrid` field containing the card IDs of non-null slots on the street grid at the end of the run. The field is nullable (backward-compatible).
- **Synergy type map is constructed from card templates** — a `Record<string, string[]>` mapping each card ID to its list of synergy types (from `MainStreetCardsTemplates`). Cards with multiple synergy types count for each type in the HHI computation (multi-type card with types A and B contributes +1 to type A count and +1 to type B count).
- **A balance report script produces G4/HHI per difficulty** — running `npx vite-node src/scripts/balance/synergy-diversity-report.ts --seeds 200 --maxTurns 40 --difficulty Medium --json` produces JSON output with HHI and type share distribution for each difficulty level (Easy, Medium, Hard). Output is also written to a markdown file (`docs/dev/assets/synergy-diversity-report.md`) with a summary table.
- **Dominance is flagged** — any synergy type with share > 40% in any difficulty is highlighted in the report output (stderr and markdown). A warning line is emitted per dominance finding.

## Constraints

- **No engine changes.** This task only adds data capture and reporting; it must not modify game engine rules, synergy formula, or card data.
- **Backward compatibility.** Adding `finalGrid` to `MonteCarloRunSummary` must be optional/nullable so existing code that does not populate it continues to work.
- **Performance.** Adding `finalGrid` capture (a shallow copy of non-null grid entries) per run should add negligible overhead (< 1ms per run).
- **Canonical profile.** The report should default to the canonical profile: 200 seeds, 60 max turns, `greedy` strategy — matching the rebalance evidence baseline. The `--maxTurns` flag should accept override.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Add `finalGrid?: string[]` to `MonteCarloRunSummary`; capture grid state at end of `simulateSeed`; handle competitive runs too.
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/global-metrics.ts` — Update `computeSynergyDiversity` to accept `Record<string, string[]>` (array of types per card) and handle multi-type cards.
- `src/scripts/balance/synergy-diversity-report.ts` — New report script (patterned after `competitive-placement-report.ts`).
- `tests/main-street/balance/global-metrics.test.ts` — Update G4 test for multi-type card handling.
- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-run-summary-extensions.test.ts` — Add test for `finalGrid` capture.

## Related Work

- **MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3** — Parent work item: Main Street rebalance evaluation.
- **docs/dev/further-balancing-recommendations.md §3 & R5** — Source of this work item. The rebalance analysis flagged synergy distortion as acceptable but needing monitoring.
- **MS-0MUQUBKNE007NYR8** — Parent: Further-balancing-recommendations artefact.
- **MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE** — Related rebalance tuning (reputation sources); completed.
- **MS-0MUYK5BEC007L61X** — Generate Mermaid diagrams for card synergies (open, low priority, unrelated).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** Multi-type cards count for each of their synergy types in the HHI denominator. This is the most defensible interpretation: a card occupying a grid slot provides all of its synergy types simultaneously, so each type should get credit.
- **Assumption:** The canonical Monte Carlo profile uses `mc-balance` seed prefix and `GreedyStrategy` for all seats — matching the existing rebalance baseline. If the competitive profile (multi-player) is needed, `finalGrid` must also be captured in competitive runs.
- **Risk:** Capturing `finalGrid` on every run adds memory pressure if runs are not garbage-collected promptly. Mitigation: store only card ID strings (not full card objects), and do the copy inline rather than holding references.
- **Risk:** If `finalGrid` is missing from existing stored run summaries (legacy data), the function degrades gracefully to `null` — no action needed.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

No interview conducted — this work item was auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker. All technical details were derived from repo inspection of:

- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Monte Carlo harness, run summary structure, grid state access.
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/global-metrics.ts` — Existing `computeSynergyDiversity` implementation.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `SynergyType` definition, card interfaces with `synergyTypes`.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — Card template loading from CSV, synergy type data.
- `src/card-data.csv` — 39 business/community cards, 10 multi-type.
- `tests/main-street/balance/global-metrics.test.ts` — Existing G4 unit tests.
- `docs/dev/further-balancing-recommendations.md` — Source specification (R5).

# Intake Brief: Static docs site for local browsing (VitePress)

**Priority: Low** | **Type: Chore** | **Assignee: Map**

> Discovered from MS-0MUNB54KU005084C as the deferred option (B). Producer
> answers 2026-10-17: still wanted (Q1=A); **navigation-first** use case
> (Q2=A); **local dev tool only**, no CI publishing (Q3=B).

## Headline

Add a VitePress static docs site over the existing `docs/game/` and
`docs/dev/` trees so developers and content authors can browse the docs with
sidebar navigation and rendered Mermaid locally (`npm run docs`); no CI
publishing is required.

## Problem statement

The repo ships docs as a flat, two-tree Markdown forest (`docs/game/`,
`docs/dev/`). Without a site, readers must navigate raw files and there is no
sidebar nav, no search, and no unified landing page. Mermaid fences in docs
(`core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `the-build-gdd.md`) render only with a
Mermaid-aware viewer. A static docs site fixes browsing and renders Mermaid at
build time.

## Users

- **Developers** — need to browse game + dev docs with nav/search while
  working on the codebase.
  - *"As a developer, I want a docs site with sidebar navigation, so I can
    find the right doc faster without guessing file paths."*
- **Game designers / content authors** — need the gameplay reference plus the
  storyline graphs readable in place.
  - *"As a content designer, I want Mermaid diagrams rendered in the docs
    page, so the storyline shape is visible without a Mermaid tool."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Docs site generator** — `vitepress` (MIT) is added as a devDependency
   and a `npm run docs` script serves the docs site locally
   (`vitepress dev docs`); the site root is `docs/` and covers both the
   `docs/game/` and `docs/dev/` trees with sidebar navigation. The
   `docs/.vitepress/` build output is git-ignored and the toolchain stays a
   devDependency only (it never enters the game bundle).
   *Metric: `npm run docs` starts a local server; `npm run docs:build`
   (`vitepress build docs`) exits 0 and emits a static site; `git status`
   stays clean after a build.*
2. **Navigation** — a sidebar (`.vitepress/config.ts`) lists the `docs/game/`
   and `docs/dev/` documents with clear audiences; every top-level `.md` in
   both trees is reachable from the nav (no orphaned docs).
   *Metric: a test asserts every `.md` under `docs/game/` + `docs/dev/` is
   covered by the sidebar config.*
3. **Mermaid rendering** — mermaid code fences in docs render to visible
   diagrams in the built site; the existing committed storyline SVGs
   (`docs/game/assets/storyline-graph-*.svg`) remain usable and are linked or
   embedded as today.
   *Metric: `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` and `the-build-gdd.md`
   render with visible diagrams in the built site.*
4. **No link breakage / no migration** — existing files stay in place under
   `docs/game/` and `docs/dev/`; existing relative links between docs keep
   working; the `docs-path-drift` guard test stays green (no
   `docs/main-street/` or `example-games/main-street/` strings in the new
   VitePress config).
   *Metric: full suite passes including `docs-path-drift.test.ts`.*
5. **Testing/validation** — a pure config-scan unit test validates the docs
   build config (nav coverage + no forbidden paths) with no
   Playwright/browser requirement, and the full project test suite passes
   with the new changes.
   *Metric: the nav-coverage test runs in the `unit` project and asserts every
   top-level `.md` under both trees is listed in the sidebar; `npm test` exits
   0.*
6. **All related documentation is updated** — `docs/README.md` (and/or a new
   `docs/index.md`) documents the docs site plus the `npm run docs` /
   `npm run docs:build` commands, and the README reflects the new scripts.
   *Metric: `docs/README.md` or `docs/index.md` mentions `npm run docs`, and
   the project README documents the docs scripts.*
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.
8. **Local-only, no CI** — no GitHub Pages or docs CI workflow/job is added;
   the `docs` scripts are for local use and the existing game Pages deploy
   workflow is unchanged.
   *Metric: no new or modified workflow file references the docs build; the
   existing deploy workflow is untouched.*
9. **Permissive licence** — `vitepress` and every new plugin/dependency are
   permissively licensed (MIT/Apache-2.0/CC0).
   *Metric: each new dependency's licence is checked and recorded in the
   implementation notes.*

## Constraints

- **Local-only, no CI** — no GitHub Pages workflow, no docs CI job
   (Q3=B). `docs` scripts are for local use; the existing game Pages deploy
   workflow is untouched.
- **Permissive licence** — `vitepress` (MIT) and any new plugin must be
   permissively licensed (MIT/Apache-2.0/CC0).
- **devDependency only** — the docs toolchain must not enter the game bundle.
- **No reorganisation** — files stay under `docs/game/` / `docs/dev/`; the
   two-tree structure and `docs/README.md` index remain.
- **Drift guard** — new VitePress files under `docs/` must not contain
   `example-games/main-street/` or `docs/main-street/` (scanned by
   `docs-path-drift.test.ts`).
- **Determinism/coverage** — the nav-coverage test must be stable and fast
   (no Playwright/browser requirement for the unit suite).

## Existing state (repo research)

- No docs-site generator present: devDeps include `vite`, `vitest`,
   `playwright`, `mermaid`, `sharp`, `tsx`, `vite-node`, but **no
   `vitepress`/`docusaurus`/`mkdocs`** anywhere in the repo or `core/`.
- `docs/` is plain Markdown: `docs/README.md` index, `docs/game/` (11 files +
   `storylines/` (5) + `assets/` with 5 storyline SVGs), `docs/dev/` (21 files +
   `assets/` (9) + `analysis/`).
- Mermaid fences exist in `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (:162),
   `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (:207, :617); the storyline graph
   ships as committed SVGs under `docs/game/assets/`.
- `docs-path-drift.test.ts` scans every text file under `docs/` for
   forbidden legacy paths; a `.vitepress/config.ts` (or `.mjs`) is a `.ts`
   text file and will be scanned — it must avoid those strings.
- Node v22.22.1 (VitePress requires Node ≥18 — satisfied).
- `.gitignore` has `dist/` and `dist-electron/`; VitePress build output
   (`docs/.vitepress/dist`) must be ignored (add `.vitepress` or
   `docs/.vitepress/dist`).

## Desired change

1. Add `vitepress` (devDependency) and a `docs` npm script.
2. Add `docs/.vitepress/config.ts` with sidebar nav for both trees
   (or `.mjs` if TS config is awkward with the repo's toolchain — prefer
   `.ts` since Vite toolchain is already TS).
3. Theme/plugin for Mermaid rendering (e.g. via the `vitepress-plugin-mermaid`
   or a mermaid pre-render step) so mermaid code fences become visible
   diagrams in the built site.
4. Add a nav-coverage test (`tests/main-street/`) asserting every top-level
   `.md` in both trees appears in the sidebar config, plus the drift-guard
   string check on the new config files.
5. Update `docs/README.md` (or add `docs/index.md`) to note the docs site and
   the `npm run docs` command.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `package.json` — add `vitepress` devDependency + `docs` / `docs:build` npm
  scripts.
- `docs/.vitepress/config.ts` — **new** VitePress config (title, sidebar,
  mermaid plugin).
- `docs/.vitepress/theme/…` and/or mermaid plugin wiring — **new**.
- `tests/main-street/docs-site-nav.test.ts` — **new** nav-coverage + drift-
  string test.
- `tests/main-street/docs-path-drift.test.ts` — existing drift guard; must
  stay green for the new `.vitepress` files.
- `.gitignore` — ignore `docs/.vitepress/` build output.
- `docs/README.md` and/or new `docs/index.md` — site introduction + `npm run
  docs` command.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUNB54KU005084C** — Render the storyline graph (Mermaid→SVG) — completed (v0.1.19); this item is its deferred option (B).
- **MS-0MUYLLYX80090370** — Link & document the rendered storyline graph — completed; embedded the SVG in the canonical doc and documented regeneration.
- **MS-0MUZK0OWJ000PQ2D** — Restructure documentation (two-tree split) — established `docs/game/` + `docs/dev/`.
- **MS-0MUNC8AOL0092BE5** — Fix stale `example-games/main-street` paths — owner of the `docs-path-drift` guard.
- **MS-0MUSY1M1F003IS47** — Editor host & read-only graph viewer (blocked) — may eventually consume the docs-rendered graphs.

## Assumptions

- The docs site is **local-only** (Q3=B): no CI build or Pages publishing is
  added; if publishing is wanted later it is a follow-up item.
- Navigation is the primary need (Q2=A); Mermaid fences are rendered in the
  built site (client-side rendering acceptable — see risk) and do not replace
  the committed `.mmd`/SVG pipeline.
- `nodemon`/live-reload behaviour from VitePress dev server is fine; no
  custom theme is needed beyond Mermaid support.

## Risks

- **Toolchain adoption (LOW–MED).** VitePress is Vite-native (repo already
  uses Vite), but its config adds a new docs toolchain. *Mitigation:*
  devDependency only; config kept small; no bundler changes.
- **Mermaid rendering approach (MED).** `vitepress-plugin-mermaid` renders
  client-side in the browser by default, not at build time; the item title
  says "at build time". *Mitigation:* either pre-render server-side (run the
  existing `mermaid` + Playwright render step during `docs:build`) or accept
  client-side rendering for the local dev use case (Q3=B); record the choice
  in the item at implementation.
- **Drift-guard interference (LOW).** New `.vitepress` files are scanned by
  `docs-path-drift.test.ts`. *Mitigation:* keep the forbidden strings out of
  new config; nav test covers coverage.
- **Scope creep risk.** Full-text search, versioning/multi-version docs,
  CI publishing, i18n, custom theming → out of scope; record as separate
  work items if requested.
- **Test determinism (LOW).** Nav test must not require a browser; keep it a
  pure config-scan unit test.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Still wanted?** Now that the minimal render step is shipped, is the
  larger static docs site still desired?
  - Options: (A) Still want it; (B) No longer needed.
  - **Recommended: (B).** Original problem solved by MS-0MUNB54KU005084C.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): (A)** — still build the static docs
    site. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Primary use case?**
  - Options: (A) Better navigation/structure; (B) Mermaid-at-render for all
    docs; (C) Both.
  - **Recommended: (A).**
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): (A)** — navigation-first; Mermaid
    rendering at build time remains in the title/scope but is not the sole
    driver. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Target audience / delivery?**
  - Options: (A) Internal/CI only (Pages); (B) Local dev tool (`npm run
    docs`); (C) Both.
  - **Recommended: (A).**
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): (B)** — local dev tool only; **no CI
    publishing**. Source: interactive reply.

> All three answers recorded in comment MS-C0MVBVDIK0006YSM7.

## Open Questions (from plan review)

- **OPEN QUESTION — build-time vs client-side Mermaid rendering.** The title
  says "render Mermaid docs at build time", but the Risks section permits
  client-side rendering for the local-only use case (Q3=B). Directed to the
  producer. Why it matters: a build-time pre-render needs a
  Playwright/Chromium step in `docs:build` (slower, more moving parts), while
  a client-side plugin keeps the build simple but ships Mermaid JS to the
  browser. Proposed default (does not block planning): client-side
  `vitepress-plugin-mermaid`, with the choice recorded in the item at
  implementation.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-19 — `/skill:plan` run: effort/risk pre-check returned **skip**
  (Extra Small, Low risk), so no decomposition was performed. Six-stage
  review applied conservatively: AC alignment (AC1 now covers the gitignore
  and devDependency-only constraints; AC8 added for local-only/no-CI; AC9 for
  permissive licence; AC5/AC6 tightened to measurable criteria), completeness
  (added the existing `docs-path-drift.test.ts` guard to Key Files),
  testability (nav test pinned to the `unit` project, no browser), polish
  (fixed the `vitepress build docs` typo). Open Question raised on build-time
  vs client-side Mermaid rendering.

# Intake Brief: Generate Mermaid diagrams for card synergies, staff relationships and upgrade chains (MS-0MUYK5BEC007L61X)

**Priority: Low** | **Type: Feature** | **Assignee: Map**
**Producer decisions (2026-10-07, interactive): Q1 = A (docs/tooling artefacts); Q2 = B (named three + community-space extension); Q3 = A (committed `.mmd` + `--check` drift guard).** See Appendix.

## Problem statement

The repo already generates a deterministic Mermaid flowchart of the storyline
graph (`src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` → `docs/dev/assets/storyline-graph.mmd`,
with a JSON manifest and a `--check` drift guard), but no other card dataset is
visualised. Designers, reviewers and new contributors must reconstruct card
synergies, staff coverage, upgrade chains and community-space relationships by
reading 174 CSV rows. Generating the same class of deterministic Mermaid
diagram for these datasets makes each relationship legible at a glance and
keeps the pictures drift-guarded against `src/card-data.csv`.

## Users

- **Content designer / producer** — sees at a glance which cards share a synergy,
  which staff can serve which businesses, and how upgrade chains branch and gate.
  - *"As a designer, I want a Mermaid diagram of card synergies, so I can check
    that every synergy type has a healthy cluster of cards without reading the CSV."*
  - *"As a designer, I want a diagram of staff coverage, so I can spot uncovered
    business types or overly broad staff."*
  - *"As a designer, I want a diagram of upgrade chains, so I can see the two-step
    level-1 → level-2 branches and their gates."*
- **Reviewer / balancer** — trusts the committed diagrams because a drift guard
  fails when they fall out of sync with `src/card-data.csv`.
- **New contributor / developer** — uses the diagrams as an entry point to the
  card model, alongside `card-catalog.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Diagram generator CLI.** A new dev-only npm script (e.g. `npm run
   docs:diagrams`) generates Mermaid from `src/card-data.csv` through the typed
   card model under `vite-node`, supporting `--diagram
   <synergies|staff|upgrades|community-spaces|all>` (default `all`), `--format
   mermaid|json` (default `mermaid`), `--out <path>` and `--check` (drift guard:
   exit `1` on drift, `0` when up to date). Verified by unit tests that invoke
   the CLI and assert its exit codes and output.
2. **Committed artefacts & drift guard.** Four deterministic Mermaid artefacts
   are committed under `docs/dev/assets/` — `card-synergies.mmd`,
   `staff-relationships.mmd`, `upgrade-chains.mmd`,
   `community-space-relationships.mmd` — and a Vitest drift guard regenerates
   each from `src/card-data.csv` and fails when the committed file differs
   byte-for-byte. The existing `storyline-graph.mmd` drift guard continues to pass.
3. **Card synergy diagram content.** Shows every business and community-space
   card and all six synergy types (Food, Culture, Service, Commerce,
   Entertainment, Health), with an edge per card↔synergy membership so cards that
   can chain adjacency bonuses are identifiable. Verified by unit tests asserting
   the exact node set plus edges for representative multi-synergy cards (e.g.
   `biz-cafe` → Food + Culture; `cs-public-art` → Culture + Entertainment) and
   that all six synergy types appear.
4. **Staff relationship diagram content.** Shows every staff card, each synergy
   type and named business it may serve (`allowedBusinessTypes`, resolved through
   the existing `getAllowedBusinessTypesForStaff` / `staffMatchesBusiness`
   helpers), and the specialization-skill catalog from `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts`
   (categories and skills). Verified by unit tests asserting representative staff
   edges (e.g. `staff-health-safety` → Health only; `staff-chef` →
   Cafe/Diner/Delicatessen/Food) and that every catalog skill appears.
5. **Upgrade chain diagram content.** Shows each upgradeable business/community
   space as a chain root plus each applicable upgrade, ordered by
   `requiredLevel`/`maxLevel` and labelled with `newDisplayName`, so level-1
   branches and the level-2 gate are visible. Verified by unit tests asserting the
   four level-2 chains (e.g. Bakery → Patisserie / Bread Factory → Grand
   Bakehouse) and that a level-2 upgrade is only shown after a level-1 step.
6. **Community-space diagram content.** Shows each of the eight community-space
   cards, its synergy types and any community-space upgrade (`targetBusiness`),
   including ongoing cost/buff fields where set. Verified by unit tests asserting
   all eight cards and their types.
7. **Determinism & safety.** Two builds from the same CSV are deeply equal, output
   is sorted and contains no timestamp/RNG/wall-clock input, the generator adds no
   runtime dependency (dev tooling only), and Mermaid remains the source of truth
   (artefacts are never hand-edited). Verified by unit tests.
8. **Documentation.** A new `docs/game/card-diagrams.md` documents every
   diagram (what it shows, how to read it) and the regeneration command, and
   `docs/game/card-catalog.md`, `docs/game/storylines.md` and
   `src/README.md` link to it. All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
   entries.
9. **Tests, build and full suite.** `npm run build` succeeds and the full project
   test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Mermaid is the source of truth.** The committed `.mmd` files are generated
  artefacts; never hand-edited. `src/card-data.csv` is the data source.
- **No new runtime dependency.** The generator is dev tooling only, mirroring
  `storylines:graph`; nothing enters the game bundle.
- **Determinism.** Sorted node/edge order, no RNG, timestamps or wall-clock input;
  byte-identical on re-run.
- **Read-only over data.** Do not change the card model, CSV schema/column order,
  or gameplay data; consume the existing typed getters
  (`getBusinessTemplates`, `getCommunitySpaceTemplates`, `getUpgradeTemplates`,
  `getStaffCardTemplates`) and `MainStreetStaffSkills`.
- **Rendering is out of scope.** SVG/PNG rendering of Mermaid stays with
  `MS-0MUNB54KU005084C`; this item commits `.mmd` (and offers `--format json` on
  demand only).
- **Scope guard.** Additional diagram domains beyond the four named (plus the
  already-existing storyline graph) are separate work items; record them rather
  than absorbing them here.
- **UK English** in all generated labels and documentation.
- **No CHANGELOG.md edits** (managed by the ship/release pipeline).

## Existing state (repo research)

- **Generator precedent.** `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` builds a
  deterministic manifest and renders Mermaid; `src/scripts/storyline-graph-cli.ts`
  is the `vite-node` entry (`npm run storylines:graph`); `tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts`
  holds the existing byte-for-byte drift guard.
- **Typed getters.** `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` exposes
  `getBusinessTemplates`, `getCommunitySpaceTemplates`, `getEventTemplates`,
  `getUpgradeTemplates`, `getStaffCardTemplates` (re-exported via
  `src/MainStreetCards.ts`).
- **Data.** `src/card-data.csv` — 174 rows: 31 business, 39 upgrade, 25 staff,
  8 community-space, 71 event. Synergy types: Food, Culture, Service, Commerce,
  Entertainment, Health.
- **Synergies.** `BusinessCard`/`CommunitySpaceCard` carry `synergyTypes`,
  `synergyCoinBonus`, `synergyRepBonus`; staff `skill-network`/`skill-tech-guru`
  modify adjacency behaviour.
- **Staff.** `staff.allowedBusinessTypes` mixes synergy types and specific
  business names (e.g. `Cafe|Diner|Food|Delicatessen`); resolved by
  `getAllowedBusinessTypesForStaff` / `staffMatchesBusiness`. Specialization
  skills live in `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` (category + effect).
- **Upgrades.** `upgrade.targetBusiness` + `upgrade.requiredLevel` + business
  `maxLevel`; `upgrade.newDisplayName` names the upgraded form. Four level-2
  upgrades gate on a level-1 parent (`upg-grand-bakehouse`, `upg-restaurant`,
  `upg-multiplex`, `upg-luxury-retreat`).
- **Community spaces.** Eight cards with `synergyTypes` and community-space
  upgrades (e.g. `upg-orchard` → Community Garden).
- **Docs.** `docs/game/card-catalog.md` catalogues cards; `docs/game/storylines.md`
  documents the storyline graph tooling and links `storyline-graph.mmd`;
  `src/README.md` references the scripts; there is **no** `card-diagrams.md` and
  no diagram for synergies/staff/upgrades/community spaces.

## Desired change

1. Add a deterministic diagram generator (`src/scripts/card-diagrams.ts` + CLI)
   that builds, for the four domains, a node/edge manifest from the typed card
   model and renders Mermaid, reusing the storyline-graph conventions
   (deterministic ordering, `--check`, `--format`, `--out`).
2. Commit the four `.mmd` artefacts under `docs/dev/assets/` (alongside `storyline-graph.mmd`).
3. Add an npm script (`docs:diagrams`) and a Vitest drift guard for each
   artefact.
4. Document the diagrams and the regeneration workflow, and cross-link from
   `card-catalog.md`, `storylines.md` and `src/README.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scripts/card-diagrams.ts` — **new**: manifest builders and Mermaid renderers for synergies, staff, upgrades and community spaces (deterministic; mirrors `storyline-graph.ts`).
- `src/scripts/card-diagrams-cli.ts` — **new** `vite-node` CLI entry with `--diagram`, `--format`, `--out`, `--check`.
- `package.json` — add the `docs:diagrams` script.
- `docs/dev/assets/card-synergies.mmd` — **new** committed artefact.
- `docs/dev/assets/staff-relationships.mmd` — **new** committed artefact.
- `docs/dev/assets/upgrade-chains.mmd` — **new** committed artefact.
- `docs/dev/assets/community-space-relationships.mmd` — **new** committed artefact.
- `docs/game/card-diagrams.md` — **new**: diagram guide + regeneration commands.
- `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — link the diagrams.
- `docs/game/storylines.md` — cross-reference the unified diagram tooling (§5/§11).
- `src/README.md` — document the new script and artefacts.
- `tests/main-street/card-diagrams.test.ts` — **new**: determinism, content-correctness and drift-guard tests.
- `src/MainStreetCards.ts` / `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — read-only reuse of the typed getters.
- `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — read-only specialization-skill catalog source.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0** — Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema (completed) — the generator/drift-guard pattern this item mirrors.
- **MS-0MUNB54KU005084C** — Render the storyline graph (Mermaid to SVG) in the docs build (open) — owns Mermaid→SVG rendering; out of scope here.
- **MS-0MUYK064P0032374** — Static docs site that renders Mermaid docs at build time (open) — a future rendering surface for these artefacts.
- **MS-0MUNB5D7K001GH19** — Visual storyline authoring editor (open, epic) — an interactive graph viewer; potential consumer of the diagram model.
- **MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY** — Canonical docs, cross-references & doc-drift guard (completed) — docs conventions this item follows.
- **MS-0MUDYQQ2E00913QN** — Synergy tooltop (completed) — established synergy-type player-facing semantics.
- **MS-0MUR9INHX001QCSE** — Track synergy diversity (G4/HHI) and placement dominance post-rebalance (open) — analytical use of the same synergy data.
- **MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4** — Level-2 upgrade prerequisite gate blocks expensive-tier adoption in greedy Monte Carlo (in-progress) — the level gate visualised in the upgrade chain diagram.

### Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** – write storylines (open)
- **MS-0MULWEEE8007J2TB** – Fix Accountant refreshCostDiscount value to ×100 scale (completed)
- **MS-0MTIIKVJE006GRQY** – Competitive state model: per-player resources, owner-tagged street (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — matched: chains, synergies, staff, upgrades, requiredlevel, maxlevel, specialization (+26 more)
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: diagram, generate, graph, manifest, card, staff, upgrades (+35 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: diagram, generate, graph, manifest, card, staff, upgrades (+31 more)

> The keyword matches above are low-precision (shared vocabulary); the manual **Related work** list is the authoritative set. Full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-MS-0MUYK5BEC007L61X.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep (MEDIUM).** "Any other sensible information" invites unbounded diagrams. *Mitigation:* fix the set at the four named domains plus the existing storyline graph; extra domains become separate work items.
- **Diagram readability (MEDIUM).** A 31-business synergy graph can become dense. *Mitigation:* group by synergy type (central type nodes), keep labels compact (name + id), and offer `--diagram` for per-domain output.
- **Upgrade-chain modelling (MEDIUM).** `requiredLevel` + `maxLevel` encode a graph that can branch (Bakery has two level-1 options and one level-2). *Mitigation:* model chains by `targetBusiness` + `requiredLevel`, assert the four level-2 chains explicitly in tests.
- **Staff target ambiguity (LOW).** `allowedBusinessTypes` mixes synergy types with business names. *Mitigation:* resolve through the existing helpers and distinguish node kinds in the diagram/tests.
- **Drift staleness (LOW).** Committed diagrams can diverge from the CSV. *Mitigation:* per-artefact `--check` drift guard.
- **Assumption** — "diagrams" means committed Mermaid artefacts in the docs, not an in-game viewer (Q1 = A).
- **Assumption** — the four named domains plus the community-space extension are the v1 set (Q2 = B).
- **Assumption** — `.mmd` is committed and drift-guarded; `--format json` is available on demand but not committed (Q3 = A).
- **Assumption** — CHANGELOG is managed by the release pipeline and is out of scope.


## Plan (2026-10-16)

Decomposed into six child features (test-first, vertical-slice order). Each
feature carries its own unit tests, committed artefact and doc updates so every
step is an end-to-end slice; later domains build on the core established by
Feature 1. Dependency edges are recorded in `wl`.

1. **Diagram generator core + CLI + synergy diagram** (tracer bullet) — generalise the
   `storyline-graph` conventions into `src/scripts/card-diagrams.ts` + `card-diagrams-cli.ts`
   with `--diagram`, `--format`, `--out`, `--check`; deliver the card-synergy domain
   end-to-end with the `docs:diagrams` npm script, committed artefact, drift guard and tests.
2. **Community-space relationship diagram** — community-space nodes, synergy edges and
   `targetBusiness` upgrades, reusing the core builder.
3. **Staff relationship diagram** — staff cards, resolvable allowed business/synergy
   targets (`getAllowedBusinessTypesForStaff`) and the `STAFF_SKILL_CATALOG`.
4. **Upgrade chain diagram** — chain roots, `requiredLevel` ordering, level-2 gates.
5. **Unified diagram documentation & cross-links** — `docs/game/card-diagrams.md` plus
   links from `card-catalog.md`, `storylines.md` and `src/README.md`.
6. **Integration, determinism & full-suite verification** — cross-domain `--check`,
   no-timestamp/no-RNG assertions, `npm run build` and the full suite green.

**Path correction (repo ground truth).** The intake brief predicted
`docs/main-street/**`, which does not exist. The shipped storyline precedent
commits its generated artefact at `docs/dev/assets/storyline-graph.mmd` and its
prose docs under `docs/game/` (`card-catalog.md`, `storylines.md`). The plan
therefore commits the four new `.mmd` artefacts under `docs/dev/assets/` and the
new guide under `docs/game/card-diagrams.md`; the corrected paths are reflected
in the Acceptance Criteria and Key Files above. Producer decision Q1=A
("mirror `storylines:graph`") makes this the unambiguous reading; recorded here
as a traceable correction rather than a new requirement.

**Scope note.** Additional diagram domains beyond the four named (plus the
existing storyline graph) remain separate work items per the scope guard.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Delivery surface: where do the diagrams live?** Options: (A) docs/tooling artefacts (committed `.mmd` under `docs/main-street/`, mirroring `storylines:graph`); (B) in-game player-facing Mermaid viewer; (C) both. **Recommended: (A).** **Answer (producer, 2026-10-07): (A)** — docs/tooling artefacts. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Diagram scope.** Options: (A) the three named domains only; (B) A plus a curated extension (community-space relationships and other clearly diagram-worthy data); (C) a single combined "everything" diagram. **Recommended: (B).** **Answer (producer, 2026-10-07): (B)** — named three plus the community-space extension. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Output and guarding.** Options: (A) deterministic committed `.mmd` plus a `--check` drift guard per diagram; (B) on-demand only, no committed artefacts or guard; (C) A plus rendered SVG/PNG (overlaps `MS-0MUNB54KU005084C`). **Recommended: (A).** **Answer (producer, 2026-10-07): (A)** — committed `.mmd` + `--check` drift guard; SVG rendering stays with `MS-0MUNB54KU005084C`. Source: interactive reply.

Research note (agent, no producer input needed): the storyline generator
(`src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts`) is the established pattern (`--format`,
`--out`, `--check`, deterministic ordering, committed artefact + drift test);
the typed template getters for business/community-space/upgrade/staff already
exist; and no synergy/staff/upgrade/community-space diagram exists today.

- **Q4 — Artefact/doc location (agent-resolved, no producer input required).**
  The brief's predicted `docs/main-street/**` paths do not exist in the repo. Repo
  research shows the storyline artefact is committed at
  `docs/dev/assets/storyline-graph.mmd` and the prose docs live under `docs/game/`.
  **Answer (agent):** commit the four `.mmd` artefacts under `docs/dev/assets/`
  and the guide under `docs/game/card-diagrams.md`, consistent with Q1=A
  ("mirror `storylines:graph`"). Evidence: `docs/dev/assets/storyline-graph.mmd`,
  `docs/game/card-catalog.md`, `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts:637`. No
  `docs/main-street/` directory exists.

# Intake Brief: Residual Expensive-Tier Branching Upgrades Below Pick-Rate Target

**Work item:** MS-0MV035PRV002QDG4 · `task` · `low`
**Discovered from:** MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M (Re-evaluate upgrade costs/ROI after the 5-turn payback rebalance)

## Headline

Two expensive-tier level-0 branching upgrades (`upg-drive-in`, cost 700; `upg-wellness-center`, cost 900) remain at or near 0% M1 pick rate on the canonical `mc-balance` Medium profile because they compete for the single upgrade market slot with higher-weighted upgrades. This task raises their draw-weight (or adjusts cost/incomeBonus) to reach ≥5% M1 on Medium without regressing the four level-2 capstones below 5% or breaking the Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard win-rate ladder.

## Problem statement

The upgrade-deck composition lever (MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W) added `drawWeight` values to the upgrade-deck: the four level-2 capstones and their level-1 prerequisites received weight boosts (2–3× baseline), but the remaining level-0 branching upgrades — `upg-drive-in` (Cinema, cost 700) and `upg-wellness-center` (Day Spa, cost 900) — were left with no `drawWeight` (baseline = 1). These two cards compete for the single upgrade slot in the market against weighted cards (drawWeight 2–3), so their market appearance rate is too low to achieve meaningful adoption. The previous rebalance (MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M) left them unchanged to avoid over-tuning the market composition.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the expensive-tier branching path (Cinema → Drive-In, Day Spa → Wellness Center) to be a viable investment option alongside the IMAX/Resort-Spa standard path and the multiplex/luxury-retreat capstone chain.
- **Producer / designer** — wants a balanced economy where all upgrade paths are reachable, with measurable Monte Carlo evidence.
- **Developer** — wants card-data-only changes (cost/incomeBonus/drawWeight); no engine modifications.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Baseline captured.** Before/after Monte Carlo evidence (200 seeds, `mc-balance` prefix, 60 turns, greedy Easy/Medium/Hard) records M1 pick rate for `upg-drive-in` and `upg-wellness-center`.
2. **Target met.** A card-data-only change (cost/incomeBonus/drawWeight) lifts both `upg-drive-in` and `upg-wellness-center` to ≥5% M1 on Medium without regressing the four level-2 capstones (`upg-grand-bakehouse`, `upg-restaurant`, `upg-multiplex`, `upg-luxury-retreat`) below 5% M1 and without breaking the Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard win-rate ladder.
3. **Tests pass.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
4. **Fallback escalated (conditional).** If the ≥5% M1 target is unreachable by card-data-only tuning without regressing the capstones or the difficulty ladder, the shortfall is documented on this work item with before/after evidence and a follow-up work item is created to escalate (per the Constraints section).

## Constraints

- **Card data only** — no engine-rule changes. Modify `cost`, `incomeBonus`, and/or `drawWeight` in `src/card-data.csv` (or equivalent template).
- If the ≥5% M1 target is unreachable without regressing capstones or breaking the difficulty ladder, document the shortfall and escalate separately.

## Existing state

- **CSV values (current):**
  | Card | Cost | incomeBonus | drawWeight | requiredLevel | targetBusiness |
  |------|------|-------------|------------|---------------|----------------|
  | upg-drive-in | 700 | 200 | (unset = 1) | 0 | Cinema |
  | upg-wellness-center | 900 | 250 | (unset = 1) | 0 | Day Spa |
  | upg-imax | 700 | 300 | 2 | 0 | Cinema |
  | upg-resort-spa | 900 | 350 | 2 | 0 | Day Spa |
  | upg-grand-bakehouse | 900 | 350 | 3 | 1 | Bakery |
  | upg-restaurant | 1400 | 550 | 3 | 1 | Diner |
  | upg-multiplex | 1400 | 700 | 3 | 1 | Cinema |
  | upg-luxury-retreat | 1400 | 700 | 3 | 1 | Day Spa |

- `drawWeight` is read from CSV column 54 (`MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts`) into `UpgradeCard` templates (`MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`), and applied to upgrade refill selection in `MainStreetStateSetup.ts` (`upgradeDrawWeight()` / `pickWeightedUpgradeIndex()`). `MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` holds no draw-weight logic.
- The `drawWeight` mechanism (verified in source, MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W): absent → weight 1 and **never** eligibility-boosted; a declared weight is the base, **plus `UPGRADE_ELIGIBLE_DRAW_BONUS` (30)** at refill time when the card's `targetBusiness` is on the street at exactly `requiredLevel` and not yet maxed. Selection is one `rng()` cumulative-weight pick over the shuffled deck (`-1` → legacy `pop()` fallback). So declaring a weight on these two level-0 cards (Cinema / Day Spa target, `requiredLevel` 0) makes them surface aggressively as soon as their target business exists — expect the tuning knob to be coarser than the raw weight number suggests, and consider a weight of 1 (declared) if the +30 bonus alone suffices.
- **Related completed work:**
  - MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M — Re-evaluate upgrade costs/ROI after the 5-turn payback rebalance (task, high)
  - MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W — Upgrade-deck composition lever: raise level-2 capstone reachability (feature, high)
  - MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4 — Level-2 upgrade prerequisite gate blocks expensive-tier adoption (feature, high)

## Key Files (validated 2026-10-21)

- `src/card-data.csv` — Modify `drawWeight` column (54) for `upg-drive-in` and `upg-wellness-center`; optionally adjust `cost`/`incomeBonus`. Current values: drive-in cost 700 / incomeBonus 200 / drawWeight empty; wellness-center cost 900 / incomeBonus 250 / drawWeight empty.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — Refill draw-weight resolver and weighted pick (`upgradeDrawWeight()`, `pickWeightedUpgradeIndex()`, `UPGRADE_ELIGIBLE_DRAW_BONUS`); read-only reference — no engine changes.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — CSV column 54 → `UpgradeCard.drawWeight`; verify plumbing (no change expected).
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-draw-weight.test.ts` — Existing draw-weight/refill-selection tests; add regression tests pinning the new declared weights and the resulting selection behaviour for these two cards.
- `tests/main-street/level2-upgrade-chain.test.ts` — Pins `upg-multiplex` ← `upg-drive-in` and `upg-luxury-retreat` ← `upg-wellness-center`; ensures the weight change does not alter chain structure.
- `src/scripts/monte-carlo.ts` — Evidence runs (flags verified to exist).
- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Monte Carlo engine; no changes expected.

## Verification commands

Baseline and after-evidence (capture per difficulty, then compare):

```bash
npx tsx src/scripts/monte-carlo.ts --seed-prefix mc-balance --strategy greedy --maxTurns 60 --seeds 200 --sweep
```

Metric gates: `upg-drive-in` and `upg-wellness-center` ≥5% M1 on Medium; the four level-2 capstones (`upg-grand-bakehouse`, `upg-restaurant`, `upg-multiplex`, `upg-luxury-retreat`) ≥5% M1; win rate Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M** — Parent context: the 5-turn payback rebalance left upgrades under-valued; this is the residual fix.
- **MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W** — Established the `drawWeight` mechanism and boosted the level-1/level-2 chain cards; `upg-drive-in` and `upg-wellness-center` were intentionally left at baseline weight.
- **MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4** — Cost tuning that preceded the draw-weight mechanism; established that cost alone cannot solve reachability.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-21 — `/skill:plan` (effort Small / risk Low → below planning threshold, review-only path): added AC4 (conditional escalation fallback) traced from Constraints; corrected the `drawWeight` mechanism description and Key Files against source (`MainStreetStateSetup.ts` owns refill weighting, not `MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`; documented the +30 eligible-draw bonus); added validated verification commands; confirmed all Key Files paths exist. No child work items created (single Small task).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were raised: the intake brief already contained measurable ACs, a bounded scope (card-data only), a documented baseline state (verified against `src/card-data.csv`) and an explicit escalation fallback. Review-only planning path retained all recorded intent unchanged; the only edits add AC4 (from Constraints) and correct source references.
