# Intake Brief: Add ToneForge factories for the four intentionally factory-less SFX mappings

## Problem statement

The Main Street runtime synth currently ships 12 ToneForge factories, but 16 logical SFX keys are mapped — four keys intentionally fall back to WAV because no ToneForge factory exists for them. This work item adds real ToneForge synth factories for those four keys so the synth covers all 16 mapped keys, then removes the factory-less workaround entries.

## Users

- **Game player** — expects consistent synthetic audio for all Main Street SFX rather than a mix of synth and WAV sounds.
- **Developer** — the tutorial and gameplay emit zero `[tfAdapter] Missing tf factory` warnings for Main Street, keeping the console clean.

Example user stories:
- As a player, I want all Main Street SFX to use the ToneForge synth consistently, so the audio experience is unified.
- As a developer, I want no missing-factory warnings on the console when playing Main Street, so real issues stand out.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **All four new factories exist in the runtime synth module** — `income-positive-chime`, `income-negative-chime`, `income-neutral-chime`, and `success-fanfare` are present in `main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` (`factories` and `descriptors`), each producing a musically appropriate one-shot sound.
2. **All 16 mapped SFX keys play through the synth** — every key in `MAIN_STREET_TF_SFX_MAPPING` is handled by the synth player (no WAV fallback), verified by `tests/main-street/tfFallback.test.ts` (no factory-less assertion for these keys).
3. **Factory-less workaround lists are updated** — `MAIN_STREET_TF_FACTORYLESS_KEYS` and `MAIN_STREET_TF_FACTORYLESS_FACTORY_KEYS` in `src/sfx-tf-mapping.ts` no longer contain the four keys (the arrays become empty).
4. **Logger and tests stay consistent** — `src/tf/tfLogger.ts` `EXPECTED_FACTORYLESS_KEYS` no longer references these four keys; `tests/main-street/tutorial-console-cleanliness.test.ts` no longer asserts WAV fallback for the four keys (or asserts they play through synth instead).
5. **Full test suite passes** — all existing tests pass, including `tfFallback.test.ts` and `tutorial-console-cleanliness.test.ts`.

## Constraints

- New factories must follow the existing pattern in `main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` (one-shot voice, Tone synthesizer, appropriate musical character).
- Preserve the existing 12 factories unchanged.
- The four new sounds should be musically appropriate:
  - `income-positive-chime`: pleasant ascending chime (positive reinforcement)
  - `income-negative-chime`: descending/flat tone (negative feedback, not alarming)
  - `income-neutral-chime`: single soft note (neutral indication)
  - `success-fanfare`: short celebratory multi-note fanfare
- No changes to the engine/core beyond the runtime synth module.
- No new external dependencies.

## Existing state

- `core/src/core-engine/tf-runtime/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` — ships 12 factories with `descriptors` and `factories` exports; uses helper functions `oneShotVoice()`, `movementVoice()`, `ambienceVoice()`, etc.
- `src/sfx-tf-mapping.ts` — maps 16 keys; 4 intentionally factory-less (tracked in `MAIN_STREET_TF_FACTORYLESS_KEYS`).
- `src/tf/tfLogger.ts` — suppresses missing-factory warnings for the 4 factory-less keys.
- `tests/main-street/tfFallback.test.ts` — asserts that factory-less keys fall back to WAV.
- `tests/main-street/tutorial-console-cleanliness.test.ts` — asserts no console warnings for the factory-less keys.

## Key Files

- `core/src/core-engine/tf-runtime/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` — Add 4 new factory entries and descriptor entries.
- `src/sfx-tf-mapping.ts` — Remove 4 keys from `MAIN_STREET_TF_FACTORYLESS_KEYS`.
- `src/tf/tfLogger.ts` — No code change needed (it derives `EXPECTED_FACTORYLESS_KEYS` from the mapping dynamically), but verify.
- `tests/main-street/tfFallback.test.ts` — Remove/assertion update for the four keys (they should now play via synth).
- `tests/main-street/tutorial-console-cleanliness.test.ts` — Update any assertions that expect WAV fallback for the four keys.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUU9QYQE006NLEZ** — Activate ToneForge runtime synth: loader diagnostics + scene wiring (completed)
- **MS-0MV26MOWT004ZCQC** — Console noise when running the tutorial (completed) — silenced per-play warnings for factory-less keys
- **CG-0MUU9PSWC009CW76** — Engine contract: WAV fallback for missing factories
- **CG-0MUTU0MFE0077H0F** — Engine ToneForge foundation

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the four sounds should be synthesized (not WAV) — consistent with the synth-first approach of the runtime module.
- **Assumption:** each sound is a short one-shot (≤ 1 second) — consistent with the existing factory pattern.
- **Risk:** musical quality of synthesized sounds is subjective. Mitigation: keep sounds simple and consistent with the existing 12 factories.
- **Risk:** the runtime synth module is a static ESM file that gets bundled — adding factories should not change bundle size meaningfully.
- **Scope-creep:** adding more factory-less keys from other games is out of scope; this item covers only the four Main Street keys.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was required: the seed context plus extensive repository evidence determined scope and approach.

- Q: "What musical character should each of the four sounds have?" — Answer (inferred from names): positive-chime (pleasant ascending), negative-chime (descending/flat but not alarming), neutral-chime (soft single note), success-fanfare (celebratory multi-note). Source: work-item title + naming convention.
- Q: "Should the logger file be updated manually?" — Answer: no manual change needed — `tfLogger.ts` derives `EXPECTED_FACTORYLESS_KEYS` dynamically from `sfx-tf-mapping.ts`, so removing from the mapping list automatically removes them from the logger's suppression set. Source: repo evidence, `src/tf/tfLogger.ts` lines 35-42.

# Intake Brief — End of game stats (MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV)

## Problem statement

The Main Street **Game Over** overlay currently presents only a *static*
end-of-run snapshot (per-player rows, score breakdown, challenges). Players
cannot see **how their economy evolved turn by turn**, so they cannot tell what
worked and what did not, or learn from a failed run. This item adds per-turn
history tracking to the game state and a **third column of end-of-game
graphs** (profit per turn, cash, businesses, staff and reputation at end of
turn), with the **cash-at-end-of-turn** figure surfaced on the Summary column
and a link to the detailed stats.

## Users

- **Main Street player at game over** — wants a visual run recap instead of
  just a final number.
  - *As a player, I want to see my cash, reputation, businesses and staff
    change turn by turn, so I can understand what worked and improve my next
    run.*
- **Competitive player** — wants the same trajectory for their own seat, so a
  loss against AI can be diagnosed.
- **Balance team / designers** — benefit from a deterministic, serialisable
  per-turn series they can inspect (and reuse for analytics).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Per-turn history captured.** A new `turnStatsHistory` series records one
   snapshot per completed turn — `{ turn, coins, reputation, score, profit,
   businesses, staff }` — where `profit` is the turn's net coin delta
   (reusing the existing `weekStartCoins` snapshot). The snapshot is recorded
   on **both** the deferred (`deferResourceApplication`) and legacy end-of-turn
   paths, and is never recorded twice for the same turn.
2. **Persistence.** `turnStatsHistory` is serialised in
   `MainStreetSerializedState` and restored by `deserializeMainStreetState`;
   legacy saves without the field load with an empty history (no crash, no
   fabricated data).
3. **Graphs.** The Game Over overlay renders a **third column** containing
   composed graphs for: **profit per turn**, **cash at end of turn**,
   **businesses at end of turn**, **staff at end of turn**, and **reputation
   at end of turn**.
4. **Summary cash line + link.** The Summary column shows the final
   **Cash at end of turn** figure, and provides a link/affordance to the
   detailed stats column.
5. **Both modes and layout.** The overlay works in single-player and
   competitive mode and fits the 1280×720 viewport without text clipping or
   vertical overflow; the existing Game State and Summary content is retained.
6. **Overlay conventions.** The new UI honours the established conventions:
   Phaser-free pure model for series data, `hudContainer` parenting, depths
   199 (backdrop) / 200 (box) / 201 (interactive), everything pushed into
   `overlayObjects`; the overlay reads committed state only (no mutation),
   adds no animation (reduced-motion safe) and returns early in
   `scene.replayMode`.
7. **Testing.** Unit tests cover per-turn capture (both paths, no
   double-record), serialise/deserialise round-trip and legacy fallback, and
   the pure series model; browser tests assert the third column and the cash
   line render in both modes.
8. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Producer decisions (see Appendix):**
  - Target project is **`tce-main-street`** (the item was mis-filed in the
    ContextHub worklog; relocated as this item).
  - **Per-turn history = Option A.** The save game does **not** hold a full
    per-turn history — only the current-turn `weekStartCoins/Rep/Score`
    snapshot — so a new per-turn series must be added, **reusing the existing
    snapshot mechanism/pattern** (persisted alongside the save, legacy
    fallback).
  - **Charting = external charting library** (producer Q3 = B; e.g. Chart.js),
    not hand-rolled Phaser Graphics (A) or SVG-as-texture (C).
  - **No additional stats** beyond the five listed (producer Q4 = "No").
  - **Layout = add a third column** to the Game Over overlay (producer Q5),
    rather than a separate full-page stats screen.
- Game engine is **Phaser `4.0.0-rc.7`**; overlay rendering lives in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`.
- External chart library integration with the Phaser canvas must not regress
  headless/Monte-Carlo runs or replay mode (chart module is skipped there).
- CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** (managed by the ship pipeline); no CI/CD
  pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- **Game Over overlay:** `showGameOverOverlay()` in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — two columns (**Game State** /
  **Summary**) with a top band (title + end-reason headline) and the
  Play Again / Menu controls anchored at the panel bottom (panel is 900 px
  wide, laid out by `panelW` / `colW` / `colGap`). The pure, Phaser-free
  content model is `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts`
  (`buildGameOverPlayerRows`, `buildGameOverChallengeSummary`,
  `formatEndReason`).
- **Current-turn snapshot:** `state.weekStartCoins` / `weekStartRep` /
  `weekStartScore` are set in `executeWeekStart`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`) and serialised in
  `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`. The per-turn net row
  (`appendTurnNetRow`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`) derives the
  turn's deltas from that snapshot and logs
  `Turn <n> net: <deltas> (score: <delta>)`.
- **Ledger history:** `EconomyLedger.getHistory()`
  (`core/src/rule-engine/EconomyLedger.ts`, imported as
  `@rule-engine/EconomyLedger`) records *every mutation*, is **not
  serialised**, and is **not per-turn** — unsuitable as-is for the graphs.
- **Counts available at turn end:** businesses = non-null entries in
  `state.streetGrid`; staff = `state.staffCards.length`; cash/reputation =
  `state.resourceBank`; score = `state.finalScore`.
- **Precedent:** the Monte Carlo harness already captures a per-turn series
  (`economyHistory: [{ turn, coins, reputation, score }]`) in
  `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` for balance analytics — a useful shape to
  mirror.
- **Save/load:** `serializeMainStreetState` / `deserializeMainStreetState`
  in `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`, with legacy fallbacks for absent
  fields.

## Desired change

1. **State.** Add a `TurnStatSnapshot` interface (`turn`, `coins`,
   `reputation`, `score`, `profit`, `businesses`, `staff`) and
   `turnStatsHistory: TurnStatSnapshot[]` to `MainStreetState`; initialise it
   to `[]` in `setupMainStreetGame` / `createCompetitiveState`.
2. **Capture.** Record one snapshot at the end of each completed turn —
   covering the **deferred** path (`finishDeferredTurnClosing`, after deltas
   are applied) and the **legacy** path — so the turn's net profit is computed
   against `weekStartCoins` exactly like `appendTurnNetRow`. Guard against
   double-recording when the two paths overlap (e.g. keyed by `turn`).
3. **Persistence.** Serialise `turnStatsHistory`; on load, default to `[]`
   for legacy saves.
4. **Model.** Extend `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` with a pure
   series builder (e.g. `buildGameOverStatSeries(state)`) returning the five
   requested series plus the final "cash at end of turn" value.
5. **Render.** Add a **third column** to `showGameOverOverlay()` rendering the
   graphs via the chosen external charting library (encapsulated in a small
   helper module so the model stays Phaser-free and testable), and add the
   **Cash at end of turn** line plus a link to the stats column on the Summary
   column. Recompute `panelW` / column widths / `panelH` so all three columns
   fit the 1280×720 viewport.
6. **Guardrails.** Skip chart construction in `scene.replayMode` / headless
   mode; keep the pure model testable without booting Phaser or the chart
   library.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — Add `TurnStatSnapshot` + `turnStatsHistory`
  to `MainStreetState`.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — Initialise `turnStatsHistory: []` for
  single-player and competitive setups.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — Record the per-turn snapshot on both
  closing paths (reuse the `weekStartCoins`/`appendTurnNetRow` pattern).
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — Serialise/restore `turnStatsHistory`
  with a legacy `[]` fallback.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — New pure series builder
  (`buildGameOverStatSeries`) + final cash-at-end-of-turn value.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Third column rendering + Summary
  cash line + link; widen/rebalance the panel layout.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — **New** thin wrapper around the
  external charting library (skipped in replay/headless).
- `package.json` — Add the charting-library dependency.
- `tests/main-street/game-over-stats.test.ts` — **New** unit tests (capture,
  round-trip, legacy fallback, series model).
- `tests/main-street/game-over-overlay.test.ts` /
  `tests/main-street/game-over.browser.test.ts` — Third-column and cash-line
  assertions.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` / `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` —
  Document per-turn history and the end-of-game stats column.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM** – Provide reason for game ending (completed) — the
  epic that built the current Game Over overlay.
- **MS-0MUWE6NCA008LDXM** – Two-column Game Over overlay (completed) — the
  layout this item extends to a third column.
- **MS-0MUWE6MA30038RGY** – Game-over summary test harness (completed) — the
  fixture/helper pattern to reuse for tests.
- **MS-0MUWNTJIK009O6BZ** – Credit AI challenge completions to the AI seat
  (completed) — introduced the per-seat Game Over breakdown.
- **MS-0MUNB4ZXQ0081EX7** – Storyline coverage analytics in Monte Carlo
  harness (open) — consumes a per-turn economy series, the same shape this
  item persists.
- **Related docs:** `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (§ Activity Log —
  Effective Deltas and Per-Turn Net, § Win conditions),
  `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`.
- Automated find-related report appended below (if produced).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — external chart library vs Phaser canvas.** Chart.js needs a canvas
  context; overlaying it on the Phaser canvas and keeping it out of
  headless/replay runs needs care. *Mitigation:* isolate the library behind
  `MainStreetStatsChart.ts`, lazy-load/skip in replay/headless, verify bundle
  size.
- **Risk — deferred vs legacy capture paths** could double-record or miss the
  final turn. *Mitigation:* record keyed by `turn` in the shared closing tail,
  with targeted unit tests for both paths.
- **Risk — save/load compatibility.** *Mitigation:* legacy fallback to `[]`,
  with a round-trip + legacy test.
- **Risk — three-column overflow at 1280×720.** *Mitigation:* recompute panel
  width/height and add a browser fit assertion.
- **Assumption — competitive-mode series scope.** In single-player the five
  series describe the run's economy. In competitive mode the shared
  `resourceBank` is seat-scoped during a turn; this brief assumes the graphs
  show the **human seat's** trajectory. *Open question, recorded in the

# Remove the all-challenges win condition

**Headline:** Completing all challenges must not end the game with a win — in
single-player or competitive play — the game ends only via the score
threshold (or opt-in turn limit/losses), while completed challenges continue
to award bonus score.

## Problem statement

Today a player wins the game as soon as every active challenge is completed:
`checkEndConditions()` (single-player) and `checkCompetitiveEndConditions()`
(competitive) both short-circuit to a `'win'` with `endReason =
'all_challenges'` before the score threshold is evaluated. This is undesired
— the intended win path is the score threshold only. Completing a challenge
should remain a scoring milestone (bonus points), never a sudden end-of-game.

## Users

- **Single-player players** — a full challenge sweep should not abruptly end
  their run; the game should continue until the score threshold.
- **Competitive players (human vs AI)** — completing the shared challenge
  pool should not hand the win to the lowest-index seat; seats race to the
  effective score threshold instead.
- **Developers / test maintainers** — the retired
  `'all_challenges'` `EndReason` member and its ~20 test/UI references are
  removed so the rule surface stays truthful.

**Example user stories:**
- As a player, I expect my 3rd challenge completion to add bonus points, not
  end the game, so I can keep building toward the score threshold.
- As a competitive player, I expect the match to be decided by the score
  race, not by whoever is seat 0 when the challenge pool empties.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In single-player, completing all active challenges no longer ends the
   game: `checkEndConditions()` has no all-challenges win branch; play
   continues until score threshold / opt-in turn limit / a loss condition.
2. In competitive play, completing all shared challenges no longer declares a
   winner: `checkCompetitiveEndConditions()` has no all-completed milestone
   win; no `competitiveWinnerId` is set by it.
3. `'all_challenges'` is removed from the `EndReason` union
   (`MainStreetStateTypes.ts`) and from `END_REASON_HEADLINES`
   (`MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts`); the build compiles with no exhaustive-
   record or dead-branch errors and no remaining `all_challenges` references
   in `src/`.
4. Completed challenges still award `challengeBonusPoints` and count toward
   the score-path formula (challenge completion remains a scoring bonus, not
   an end condition).
5. Player-facing copy and current-rules docs no longer advertise an
   all-challenges win: `MainStreetHelpContent.ts`, `main.ts`, `MainStreetScene.ts`,
   `MainStreetDifficulty.ts` comments, `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`
   §7 (remove win condition item 2), and `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` end-game
   headline list.
6. Unit tests are added/updated proving that completing every active
   challenge does **not** end a single-player or competitive game (game
   `gameResult` remains playing; subsequent turns continue to the score
   threshold), and existing tests that assert an `'all_challenges'` win
   (turnflow, competitive-phase, competitive-endless,
   competitive-end-condition-ai-win, integration, game-over overlay/summary
   fixtures) are rewritten or removed. This is the primary validation
   criterion.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries
   (historical GDD/PRD documents keep their status banners and historical
   text).
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No backward compatibility requirement** for saved games carrying
  `endReason = 'all_challenges'` (operator-confirmed). `formatEndReason`
  already falls back gracefully for unknown values (underscore→space
  rendering), so a restored legacy save renders a readable generic headline
  rather than crashing.

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts:626` — `checkEndConditions()` wins via
  `activeChallenges` all-completed, sets `gameResult='win'`,
  `endReason='all_challenges'`, before the score-threshold check (which
  therefore never runs in that case; priority is documented in tests).
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts:1048` — `checkCompetitiveEndConditions()`
  has the same shared-milestone win (lowest-index seat wins via
  `competitiveWinnerId = 0`).
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts:151-162` — `EndReason` union includes
  `'all_challenges'`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts:39` — exhaustive
  `END_REASON_HEADLINES` entry; compile-time guard forces updates when the
  union changes.
- Player copy still advertises an instant win: `MainStreetHelpContent.ts`
  ("bonus points and instant-win conditions"; "games end when you win (score
  threshold / all challenges)"), `main.ts:7`, `MainStreetScene.ts:1461`,
  `MainStreetDifficulty.ts:67,85`.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §7 item 2 documents Challenge
  Completion as an automatic win; the challenges are a fixed catalogue
  (shared pool in competitive, per-seat credit with `challengeBonusPoints`).
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md:877` lists *All challenges* among game-over
  headlines.
- Tests asserting the win: `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts`,
  `competitive-phase.test.ts`, `competitive-endless.test.ts`
  (`all_challenges still wins regardless of endlessMode`),
  `competitive-end-condition-ai-win.test.ts`, `integration.test.ts`,
  `competitive-play-acceptance.test.ts`, `game-over-overlay.test.ts`,
  `game-over-summary.test.ts` / `game-over-summary-acceptance.test.ts`,
  `game-over.browser.test.ts`.

## Desired change

- Remove the two all-challenges win branches (single-player and competitive).
- Remove `'all_challenges'` from the `EndReason` union and all exhaustive
  handling; fix the endless-mode doc comment that lists it among end
  conditions.
- Keep challenge evaluation and scoring (`evaluateChallenges`,
  `challengeBonusPoints`, per-seat credit) intact.
- Update player copy, code comments, and current-rules docs.
- Rewrite/remove affected tests; add regression tests proving no
  all-challenges win in either mode.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — remove the two all-challenges win branches (lines ~626 and ~1048)
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — drop `'all_challenges'` from the `EndReason` union and fix the endless-mode comment
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — remove the `all_challenges` headline entry
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` — "instant-win" copy and "score threshold / all challenges" wording
- `src/main.ts`, `src/MainStreetScene.ts`, `src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — stale "all challenges" win references in prose
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — remove Challenge Completion from §7 win conditions
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — remove *All challenges* from the game-over headlines list
- `tests/main-street/*` — turnflow, competitive-phase, competitive-endless, competitive-end-condition-ai-win, integration, competitive-play-acceptance, game-over-overlay, game-over-summary(+acceptance), game-over.browser

## Related work

- `Provide reason for game ending (MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM)` — completed; introduced `endReason`/headlines; its exhaustive-record guard will now force this cleanup.
- `Ai should check win conditions (MS-0MUX6PMCE002I6HO)` — completed; AI win checks; no all-challenges handling.
- `Fix win/loss attribution in checkCompetitiveEndConditions (MS-0MUXLP6V00075IQY)` — completed; the competitive end-check this item modifies.
- `Competitive mode: halve the score target per AI opponent (MS-0MUUE0FVZ001VE2D)` — completed; the effective-threshold race that remains the sole competitive win path.
- `Competitive mode: divide the score target by the number of players (MS-0MUZH6V7C0091SGE)` — completed; documents the effective win threshold in §7.
- `Implement: per-seat challenge attribution (MS-0MV341FCC0028TSE)`, `Test: per-seat challenge completion attribution (MS-0MV33NV6O002WBYA)`, `When playing with AI player is credit with AI challenges (MS-0MUWNTJIK009O6BZ)` — completed; challenge credit stays intact (AC4).
- `Two-column Game Over overlay (MS-0MUWE6NCA008LDXM)` — completed; the game-over layout that renders the end-results (may surface the retired reason in fixtures).
- Duplicate check performed — no overlapping open/completed item found.
- Automated report from find-related: repo matches `docs/dev/prd-milestone-2.md`, `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md`, `core/AGENTS.md` (historical/context references to the all-challenges rule).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the score threshold remains the sole win path (plus opt-in
  turn-limit victory, last-standing in competitive); no new win condition is
  being introduced.
- **Assumption:** removing the union member is safe because saves do not
  type-check `endReason`; legacy values render via the existing fallback.
- **Risk (low):** a game where the player has completed every challenge must
  still be winnable via score — the bonus points already contribute, so no
  rebalancing is expected, but a balance sanity-check of runs where the
  challenge pool empties is prudent.
- **Scope-creep guard:** historical docs (GDD, PRD milestone 2) keep their
  "Status update" banners — only current-rules docs are edited. Any balance
  tuning discovered during implementation should be tracked as a new work
  item, not folded into this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Removal scope — which modes lose the all-challenges win?" —
  Answer (producer, interactive): "1. A — both single-player and
  competitive." Source: Skill interview round 1.
- Q2: "With the win removed, what role do challenges keep?" — Answer
  (producer, interactive): "2. A — challenges remain, awarding
  `challengeBonusPoints`; game ends only via score threshold / turn limit /
  losses." Source: Skill interview round 1.
- Q3: "How to handle the `all_challenges` `EndReason` type?" — Answer
  (producer, interactive): "3. B — remove it entirely from the type,
  headline, and tests (no backward-compatibility requirement)." Source:
  Skill interview round 1.

# Intake brief: Port the Vite watcher-ignore (`server.watch.ignored`) guard to sibling game repos' `vite.config.ts`

## Problem statement

The core scaffold template (CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA) emits `server.watch.ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS]` (covering `**/.worklog/**` and the dev-output trees), and `tce-main-street` and `tce-the-rising` already carry the block — but 8 sibling game repos' checked-in `vite.config.ts` still lack it: `AI_Hell`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-coloretto`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-golf`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-sushi-go`. When any of these repos accumulates `.worklog/worktrees/**` checkouts (AI_Hell already has 9 + a nested `ToneForge` checkout), the Vite/Vitest file watcher recursively walks them and exhausts the host `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` budget — `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached` — crashing the dev server and breaking test runs (the exact failure mode fixed in the parent item MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY).

## Users

- **Developers/agents working in any Tableau-Card-Engine game repo** (tce-\*) — must be able to run `npm run dev` and `npm test` from the main checkout once worktrees exist without tripping the host watcher limit.
  - *User story:* "As a developer in tce-blackjack, I want my dev server to ignore `.worklog/worktrees/**` so a recursive watch never exhausts inotify (ENOSPC)."
- **AI_Hell maintainers** (in scope — Q1 answered) — same failure mode is already active (9 worktree checkouts).
  - *User story:* "As an AI_Hell developer, I want the same watcher guard, so my `vite` dev server survives `.worklog/worktrees/**` growth."
- **Verification/audit tooling** — full-suite runs in sibling repos must not fail with ENOSPC.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Watcher guard present in every in-scope repo's checked-in config.** The 7 tce-\* repos each import `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` from `./core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin` and set `server.watch.ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS]` with the template's explanatory comment (wording as in CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA / `tce-the-rising`). AI_Hell (if in scope) sets `watch.ignored` from a locally defined constant covering `**/.worklog/**` (plus its dev-output trees). Verified per repo by grep of the checked-in file — no in-scope repo may lack the block.
2. **Per-repo regression guard test (mirrors the core/main-street ENOSPC guard).** Each tce-\* repo gains `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (copy of main-street's, minus the in-process dev-server smoke; static assertions only): the real config imports the shared list, spreads it into `server.watch.ignored`, and the list covers `**/.worklog/**` plus `**/data/**`, `**/tmp/**`, `**/results/**`, `**/dist/**`. AI_Hell gains `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` asserting its local list covers `.worklog`. Each test is picked up by that repo's existing test projects and passes.
3. **Surgical port only.** No other template drift is synced: no `resolvePagesBase`/`base` backfill, no blind re-scaffold (sibling configs predate those template additions), no local-config changes (e.g. AI_Hell's `configCsvPlugin`, `open: true`, port settings) altered. Per-repo `git diff` touches only `vite.config.ts` plus the new guard test; pre-existing unrelated working-tree changes (`.gitignore`, untracked `AGENTS.md`/`.githooks/`/`.worklog/plugins/`) are never swept into a commit.
4. **Suites pass and changes land on each repo's `dev`.** Each in-scope repo's own test suite passes (agent-initiated runs go through the test skill, per repo), and each repo's change is committed on its `dev` branch and pushed to origin, with commits referencing `MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0` (precedent: cross-repo item MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV). The pre-existing 1-ahead-unpushed local commit on each sibling `dev` is accounted for at push time (see Constraints). tce-main-street itself has no source changes, so its suite is unaffected; full project suite (each modified repo) must pass with the changes.
5. **Documentation reflects the guard.** Config comment matches the core template wording; where a repo documents `npm run dev` (README/dev docs — currently none of the in-scope repos has a README), a matching note about the `.worklog/**` exclusion. CHANGELOG.md excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **No core/TCE repository edits and no submodule moves.** The core scaffold template and its guard tests are already correct (CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA completed) and every sibling's pinned core commit (`09723c4b`) already exports `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` in `scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts` — verified.
- **Surgical only** — do **not** blind re-scaffold (`npm run scaffold` / `scaffold:games`): the current template additionally emits `resolvePagesBase`/production `base` behaviour that the sibling configs do not have; a re-scaffold would change more than the watch block. Port the `server.watch.ignored` block + import only.
- **Cross-repo working-tree isolation.** This item lives in tce-main-street's worklog but touches 8 sibling checkouts, all outside the tce-main-street worktree. Precedent MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV ("Cross-repo change ... Pushed to sibling dev") governs: edit each sibling checkout directly, commit per repo on its own `dev`, push per repo. tce-main-street's own worktree/main checkout stays untouched (no tce-main-street source change → no implement-worktree changes expected).
- **Respect pre-existing dirt.** Each sibling has unrelated uncommitted changes (`.gitignore` edits; untracked `AGENTS.md`, `.githooks/`, `.worklog/plugins/`). Never commit them; stage only `vite.config.ts` (+ new test).
- **Sibling `dev` is 1 commit ahead of origin** (an unpushed `.worklog/config.yaml` CTA commit, `WL-0MUWCGF670087GAS`). Pushing the port will carry that commit; if a non-fast-forward/push rejection occurs, resolve against that known baseline (do not rewrite others' pushed history).
- **Test-execution policy:** all agent-initiated test runs go through the test skill — run per repo (each sibling has its own CWD/worklog), never ad-hoc `npm test`/`vitest`.

## Existing state

- **Scaffolded siblings (7):** `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-coloretto`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-golf`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-sushi-go` — `vite.config.ts` is AUTO-GENERATED (scaffold `renderViteConfig`), identical to each other apart from the game name in the header comment, and each `server:` block has `port: 3000, open: false` only — no `watch.ignored`. Verified: `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` absent from all 7.
- **AI_Hell (1):** bespoke hand-written config (port 5173, `open: true`, `configCsvPlugin`, no `core` submodule) — no `server.watch` at all; it **cannot** import the core list. It already has 9 `.worklog/worktrees/**` checkouts (+ nested `ToneForge` checkout) — the ENOSPC failure mode is live there.
- **Exemplars:** `tce-main-street/vite.config.ts` and `tce-the-rising/vite.config.ts` already carry the block (main-street also has `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts`, the regression pattern to mirror; core has `game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` static guard).
- Siblings' core submodules are clean and pinned at `v0.1.17-201-g09723c4b`, which exports `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS`. Their `npm test` = `vitest run --project unit` with `include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts']`, and tsconfig includes `tests/**/*.ts` — new config tests are picked up automatically.

## Desired change

- **Per tce-\* repo:** in `vite.config.ts`, add `import { DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS } from './core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin';` and extend the `server:` block with `watch: { ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS] }` + the template's ENOSPC comment; add `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (static assertions copied from main-street's guard).
- **AI_Hell (in scope — Q1 answered):** add a locally defined ignore constant (e.g. `vite/watchIgnore.ts`) mirroring the core list (or a scoped `.worklog`-focused list), wire `server: { watch: { ignored: [...] } }` into `vite.config.ts`, and add `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts`.
- Single source of truth stays in core; nothing in `core/` changes.

## Key Files:

- Each tce-\* repo: `vite.config.ts` — add `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` import + `server.watch.ignored` block
- Each tce-\* repo: `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (new) — static config-wiring + pattern-coverage guard (mirror of `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` ENOSPC assertions and main-street's `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts`)
- AI_Hell: `vite.config.ts` — wire `watch.ignored`; `vite/watchIgnore.ts` (new) — local ignore constant; `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` (new) — guard test (AI_Hell test roots: `src`, `scripts`, `vite`)
- Reference only (no change): `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (template already correct), `core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts` (`DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` source), `tce-main-street/tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (guard pattern to mirror)

## Related work

- MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY — Host inotify watcher exhaustion (ENOSPC) breaks main-checkout test runs (**parent; completed**; this item is its derived sibling port)
- CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA — core: `game-repo-scaffold` renderViteConfig omits `server.watch.ignored` (completed; template now emits it)
- CG-0MTJ7A4Z3000MFMV / CG-0MTJ560IZ005XAZC — core: vite-transcript-plugin ENOSPC hardening (completed)
- MS-0MVA50KJN009X30C — [test-failure] suite-exit failure (completed; same root cause family)
- MS-0MV5PNIPO00940KG — Main Street vite-node CLI test flake (completed; the local isolation that a blind re-scaffold would regress)
- MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV — Cross-repo change precedent: tracked in main-street worklog, "Pushed to sibling dev" AC (completed)
- MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV / MS-0MUQZH53F004ZKAN — Core scaffold Pages-base work (completed; the template drift deliberately **not** backfilled here)
- Note: sibling repos have their own worklog stores (some without a DB on disk); no sibling-side work items exist for this change — the main-street item is the tracking point.

## Assumptions & risks

- **Assumption (Q1 answered: include AI_Hell):** AI_Hell is in scope, handled via a locally defined ignore constant because it has no `core` submodule from which to import the shared list.
- **Risk (low):** chokidar ignore-glob semantics — `**/.worklog/**` covers `.worklog/worktrees/**`; validated by the core regression suite and main-street's in-process smoke. Sibling guards use the same static assertions.
- **Risk (medium):** list duplication in AI_Hell drifts from core over time — mitigation: comment in `vite/watchIgnore.ts` pointing at the core source (single source of truth), and the guard test pins `.worklog` coverage.
- **Risk (medium):** per-repo dev-server smoke tests ×8 would be slow/flaky under suite contention — mitigation: ship **static** config-wiring guards per repo (mirroring `game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`); the in-process `server.watcher.getWatched()` smoke stays where it already exists (main-street) — no new dev-server startups in siblings.
- **Risk (low):** push non-fast-forward on 7 sibling `dev` branches (each 1 local commit ahead of origin) — known baseline commit; rebase/stacking acceptable since those commits are local-only; surface anything unexpected rather than force-pushing.
- **Scope-creep risk:** syncing other stale template drift (`resolvePagesBase`/production `base`, `unit-cli` isolations, etc.) to siblings, or host inotify tuning, is tempting — recorded as related work (MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV etc.), NOT this item's scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: **Is AI_Hell in scope?** Its `vite.config.ts` is hand-written (not scaffold-generated), it has no `core` submodule, so the shared `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` list cannot be imported — the port there requires a locally duplicated ignore constant (drift risk), though its failure mode is already live (9 worktrees).
  - Options: (a) **Include AI_Hell** with a local ignore constant + guard test — rec, because the producer explicitly listed it and its ENOSPC risk is already active; (b) Exclude AI_Hell — port only the 7 scaffolded tce-\* repos and file a derived item in AI_Hell's own worklog (AH- prefix); (c) Include AI_Hell only if it adopts the core submodule (large, out of scope).
  - **Recommended:** (a) Include AI_Hell with a locally defined constant (comment referencing core as canonical source), pending producer confirmation.

# Auto-sync engine submodule on dev builds; pin release builds to committed engine version

## Problem statement

`npm run build` silently compiles against whatever commit happens to be checked out in the `./core` submodule (currently `dc4ec0ce`, v0.1.21-3-gdc4ec0ce), and nothing ever updates it. Dev builds can therefore skew from the latest engine without anyone noticing, while release builds are not reproducible because nothing records which engine commit they were built against.

## Users

- **Game developer (internal)** — wants dev builds to always compose the latest Tableau Card Engine so behaviour is tested against current engine code. User story: "As a game developer, I want `npm run build` to pull the engine's latest remote HEAD, so my builds reflect current engine behaviour without manual submodule surgery."
- **Release operator (maintainer)** — wants deterministic, reproducible release builds. User story: "As a release operator, I want release builds to compile against exactly the engine SHA recorded in a committed pin file, so a release can be reproduced bit-for-bit from source."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `npm run build` (and `npm run build:electron`) runs an `engine:sync` step before compiling: `git submodule update --remote core` fetches the latest remote HEAD of whatever branch `core` tracks and checks it out. The build fails loudly (never clobbers) if `./core` has uncommitted changes.
2. `npm run build:release` runs an `engine:verify` step instead: it reads the committed pin file `configs/engine-pin.json` (engine SHA), checks out exactly that SHA, and fails the build if the pinned SHA differs from the remote-resolved target or contains local modifications.
3. `configs/engine-pin.json` holds a single `sha` field (e.g. `{"sha": "dc4ec0c..."}`) and is written only by the release process (alongside the version bump) — never by dev builds.
4. The `engine:sync` / `engine:verify` npm scripts are independently invocable (`npm run engine:sync`, `npm run engine:verify`) and covered by unit tests for the dirty-state guard and pin-mismatch failure paths.
5. The build-script template change is made in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (engine repo) and main-street is re-scaffolded so a future re-scaffold does not clobber the change. Full project test suite passes with the new changes; all related documentation (docs/dev, README/DEPLOYMENT as applicable) is updated.

## Constraints

- **No CI beyond npm builds** — there is no separate CI pipeline; `npm run build` is the verification vehicle. Release pinning is enforced at tag/merge time only, not by a CI job.
- **Scaffold ownership** — `package.json` scripts and `vite.config.ts` in main-street are scaffolded from `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (engine repo). The dev/release script change must land in that template, then main-street is re-scaffolded; editing only the generated copy gets clobbered.
- **`git submodule update --remote` must never overwrite dirty submodule state** — fail loudly instead.
- Core's remote default branch is `main`; the submodule may be checked out detached or tracking a branch — sync must behave correctly for either.

## Existing state

- `.gitmodules` declares `core` → `git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine.git`.
- `package.json` has `build: "tsc --noEmit && vite build"` and `build:electron`; no `build:release`, no engine sync/verify steps.
- Submodule currently at `dc4ec0ce` (v0.1.21-3-gdc4ec0ce), never auto-updated.

## Desired change

- Add `engine:sync` (dev auto-update + dirty guard), `engine:verify` (pin check + exact checkout), and `build:release` scripts; wire `engine:sync` into `build`/`build:electron` and `engine:verify` into `build:release`.
- Introduce `configs/engine-pin.json` owned solely by the release process.
- Update the scaffold template in the engine repo (`core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) so generated game repos get the same scripts; re-scaffold main-street.

## Key Files

- `package.json` — new `engine:sync`, `engine:verify`, `build:release` scripts; `build` / `build:electron` wiring.
- `scripts-*` (generated via `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) — new engine sync/verify script that the npm scripts invoke; located in the engine repo template and re-scaffolded into main-street.
- `configs/engine-pin.json` — new committed pin file (`{"sha": "..."}`).
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — engine-repo template to update so re-scaffolds carry the new behaviour.
- `vite.config.ts` — generated; verify re-scaffold preserves any needed changes (no manual edits expected).
- `docs/dev/*` — build/release documentation to reflect dev/release split.

## Related work

- MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV — "Core scaffold template Pages base" (completed): precedent for the cross-repo process of editing the core scaffold template and re-scaffolding this repo; the implementation consideration in this item mirrors it.
- MS-0MV5928XV0007X1J — "Cross-repo: core pack-asset byte seam + submodule bump" (completed): precedent for bumping the `core` submodule pointer as part of main-street work.
- MS-0MV76P7BN00164RF — "Toneforge should be off by default" (completed): documents the cross-repo submodule-bump discipline.
- MS-0MUQ1KXAS003FJ42 — "Ship web-based copy of Main Street (GitHub Pages)" (completed): release/deployment pipeline context.
- MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV — "Load the committed ToneForge runtime synth module" (completed): submodule-bump precedent.
- MS-0MV16VZWP001OUNR — "Full-suite verification & release readiness" (completed): release-gating precedent.
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` / `core/AGENTS.md` — engine-repo docs to update when the scaffold template changes.
- MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED risk note: a bad `engine:sync` could land a broken engine commit in dev builds; mitigation is the loud-failure dirty guard and the pin/verify split.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: auto-sync lands a broken engine commit.** Dev builds silently move to a newer engine that may be red on its own suite. Mitigation: `engine:sync` is loud about what it changed and dirty-state guard prevents clobbering; the pinned release path is the safety net.
- **Risk: dirty `./core` submodule.** `git submodule update --remote` refuses when uncommitted changes exist; we must surface that as an explicit build failure, not a silent skip.
- **Risk: network/remote dependence.** Dev builds now require reachable GitHub at build time; offline builds fall back to current checkout with a warning (assumption — confirm behaviour during implementation).
- **Risk: scope creep** — pin-file metadata (tags, dates), CI jobs, or Steam/Electron packaging integration are out of scope; record as linked work items if needed.
- **Assumption:** core's tracking branch may change; sync follows whatever branch `core` tracks (operator answer Q2-A), which matches the submodule's configured remote branch.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What should the key testable outcomes be?" — Answer (rgardler, interactive): "B — dev/release paths both produce correct results, dirty-state detection prevents accidental commits, `engine:sync` / `engine:verify` independently callable (noting: no CI outside npm builds)". Source: intake round 1.
- Q2: "How aggressive should engine:sync be?" — Answer (rgardler, interactive): "A — always fetch latest remote HEAD of whatever branch core tracks". Source: intake round 1.
- Q3: "CI impact?" — Answer (rgardler, interactive): "C — keep CI as-is; release pinning is enforced at tag/merge time only". Source: intake round 1.
- Q4: "Pin file schema?" — Answer (rgardler, interactive): "A — `{"sha": "..."}` only". Source: intake round 1.
- Q5: "Scaffold template changes?" — Answer (rgardler, interactive): "A — update in the core repo's scaffold template, then re-scaffold main-street". Source: intake round 1.
data.title: Auto-sync engine submodule on dev builds; pin release builds to committed engine version

# Extract the storyline features — the generic storyline system in TCE core

**Headline:** Move the branching storyline mechanic from tce-main-street into Tableau-Card-Engine core as a standalone, pluggable generic system; add a Gym demo scene; refactor Main Street to consume the core system while preserving current behaviour exactly.

## Problem statement

The storyline mechanic (named, multi-step incident arcs where a drawn card offers branching options and the player's decision selects the next card) lives today in tce-main-street as Main-Street-specific modules (`src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` and friends). No other TCE game can reuse it, and the engine has no generic home for branching narrative. The code was deliberately built behind an "extraction seam" (MS-0MUMP93DI0018OGV) in anticipation of this move; this work performs the move.

## Users (with user stories)

- **As a game developer building on TCE**, I want a standalone generic storyline engine (types, compilation, resolution, journal helpers, pluggable UI adapter) in core so any game can ship branching card narratives without copying Main Street code.
- **As a TCE core engineer**, I want a Gym demo scene that exercises the draw → decision → successor-chain loop so the mechanic is demonstrable and testable in isolation.
- **As a Main Street player**, I want the five shipped storylines to keep behaving exactly as they do today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Standalone generic storyline system in core** — a new core module exposes the generic types, legacy `hasChoices` and CSV `options` compilation, the registered-option registry, resolution semantics (`apply`/`skip` effect policy, successor precedence, one seeded `state.rng()` draw per candidate selection), a **pluggable UI adapter** with a default implementation, and unit tests in core proving parity with today's model tests; no Main-Street imports and no Phaser dependency.
- **Gym demo scene** — `GymStorylineScene` in `core/example-games/gym` (registered in the Gym router) where a small hand of story cards deals a branching narrative: the player draws a card, sees the options, picks one, the choice determines the next card, and the chain ends cleanly; pure logic is exercised by a unit test and the scene runs in the Gym smoke test.
- **Main Street refactored to consume core** — `MainStreetStoryline.ts`, `MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts` and `MainStreetStorylineUi.ts` re-implemented as thin adapters over the core module with the exported API surface used by callers backward-compatible; existing storyline tests in tce-main-street pass unchanged (`storyline-model`, `storyline-csv-options`, `storyline-regression-harness`, `storyline-player-agency`, `storyline-journal`, `storyline-author`, `storyline-graph`, `storyline-graph-svg`, `MainStreetEventChoiceUndo`, `validate-storylines` and the doc-drift test).
- **Behaviour preserved** — the five shipped storylines (tax, health, economy, labour, restaurant) and the CSV/card-pack authoring formats are unaffected; CSV `options` encodings authored for Main Street remain valid; RNG seed replays produce identical results.
- **Documentation** — `docs/game/storylines.md` (Main-Street view) and a new/updated core dev reference documenting the generic module, the pluggable UI adapter and the Gym demo are kept current and covered by the doc-drift guard.
- **Full test suite passes** — `npm test` in core (incl. smoke) and `npm test` in tce-main-street both green.

## Constraints

- **API parity:** the types and function signatures consumers rely on today must not change in a breaking way; the seam is the contract.
- **Determinism/replay:** RNG consumption (one seeded draw per candidate selection) must be byte-for-byte preserved.
- **Legacy equivalence:** legacy two-way choice cards compile to exactly the same two options as today.
- **Pluggable UI:** the UI seam must be an interface; core ships a default, games override. No Phaser dependency in the generic module.
- **Repo boundaries:** extraction lands in the `core` submodule (Tableau-Card-Engine). Main Street imports it via the existing `@core-*` alias mechanism.

## Existing state

- The storyline mechanic is implemented in tce-main-street: `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` (compilation + registry + resolution + pending-choice lifecycle, already documented as an extraction seam), `src/MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts` (journal + choice-clarity helpers), `src/MainStreetStorylineUi.ts` (player-agency helpers), plus types in `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` and engine integration in `src/MainStreetEngine*`/`src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`.
- Five shipped storylines, CSV `options` encoding, a storyline graph/manifest toolchain, and an extensive test suite.
- The tce-main-street repo already consumes core via aliases (`@core-engine`, `@card-system`, …) and `vite.config.ts` resolves the sibling `./core` checkout (a git submodule).

## Desired change

- Create a new core module (e.g. `core/src/story-line/` — name TBD at implementation) containing types, compilation, resolution, journal/pure helpers and the pluggable UI adapter interface, mirroring today's behaviour.
- Ship a Gym demo scene exercising the mechanic.
- Refactor tce-main-street storyline modules to delegate to the core module, keeping behaviour identical.

## Key Files:

- `core/src/story-line/…` — new generic module (types, compile, resolve, journal, ui-adapter).
- `core/example-games/gym/scenes/GymStorylineScene.ts` — new demo scene (+ Gym router registration).
- `core/tests/…` — new unit tests for the story-line module + gym scene.
- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`, `src/MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts`, `src/MainStreetStorylineUi.ts` — refactored to consume core.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — types re-exported from core (or kept in sync) for backward compatibility.
- `docs/game/storylines.md` — updated; new core dev reference for the story-line module.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** gym scene stays a proof-of-concept demo (user-confirmed); storyline *authoring editor*, *conditional/cost-gated options* (MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9) and card-pack *manifest export* are out of scope and tracked by their own work items.
- **Submodule coupling:** changes land in the `core` submodule first; tce-main-street tests only see them after the submodule is bumped — coordinate commit order (core first, then Main Street submodule pointer + refactor).
- **Behaviour drift:** risk that refactoring changes subtle semantics (RNG order, option-order, message text). Mitigation: parity tests in core + unchanged Main Street suite as the gate; review transcript strings carefully (story-update text) since those are asserted by tests.
- **Assumption:** the exported names of the three Main-Street modules remain callable as today (adapter layer), even if their bodies delegate to core.
- **Assumption:** journal/choice-clarity UI logic moves to core as pure helpers behind the UI adapter; the Main-Street overlay presentation stays game-side.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUMP93DI0018OGV** — *Storyline model & extraction seam* (completed): laid the seam this work formalises.
- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** — *write storylines* (completed): parent epic that produced the mechanic.
- **MS-0MV8KQJR30007JL5** — multi-way options / CSV `options` encoding (completed): formats that must stay valid.
- **MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9** — *Extend storyline options with conditional and cost-gated effects* (open): future extension on top of the generic system.
- **MS-0MUSY1K6B00095AT** — *Storyline editor test harness & fixtures* (open): related editor tooling, out of scope.
- **MS-0MV8KQQQ90044CM5** — *Migrate five shipped storylines* (completed): the five arcs that must keep behaving as now.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Scope of A (extraction): what parts move to core vs stay game-specific? (model/resolution → core? journal overlay UI → core? graph tools → core?)"
  Answer (rgardler, interactive reply): "Your call. We are aiming for a generic storyline system in core. It needs to be standalone so that we can build the Gym scene as a demo. Key components need to be pluggable, such as the UI."
  Research: `MainStreetStoryline.ts` is already documented as the extraction seam with migration notes; `MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts`/`MainStreetStorylineUi.ts` are pure Phaser-free helpers — portable to core behind a UI adapter. Graph/manifest tooling stays with Main Street docs/tooling (no core dependency observed). Key files: `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`, `src/MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts`, `src/MainStreetStorylineUi.ts`.
- Q: "Scope of B (gym scene): proof-of-concept demo showcasing the mechanic, or something more elaborate?"
  Answer (rgardler, interactive reply): "A" — a proof-of-concept/demo scene in the core Gym.
  Research: `core/example-games/gym/scenes/` holds per-mechanic demo scenes (e.g. `GymDeckRngScene`, `GymHandPileScene`) registered in `GymRegistry.ts`; a `GymStorylineScene` follows the same pattern.
- Q: "Existing storylines: must Main Street be refactored (not removed) to consume the core engine storyline system?"
  Answer (rgardler, interactive reply): "yes" — core provides the engine, Main Street becomes a consumer, behaviour unchanged.
  Research: Main Street already imports core via `@core-*` aliases resolved by `vite.config.ts`; the seam module was designed for exactly this delegation.

## Related work (automated report)

# Feature 2: dynamic synergy in event resolution

## Summary
When resolving `evt-grand-opening`, use the placed cards synergies from `placedSynergiesThisTurn` (union semantics) instead of the static `event.targetSynergy` in all three engine paths: `resolveEvent`, `applyCompetitiveEventEffects`, `computeOwnerEventDeltas`.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Resolve `evt-grand-opening` after a Food placement: coin delta = 450 × (grid cards sharing Food synergy), Commerce cards excluded unless they also share Food.
2. Multi-synergy placed card (`Food|Culture`): any grid card sharing any placed synergy counts (union, consistent with existing `synergyTypes.includes`).
3. Community-space placement drives the synergy selection symmetrically.
4. All three engine paths (`resolveEvent`, `applyCompetitiveEventEffects`, `computeOwnerEventDeltas`) resolve the same dynamic synergy.
5. Static `targetSynergy: Commerce` remains in `card-data.csv`; the override is a resolution-time keyword check on `evt-grand-opening`.
6. No behaviour change for other `SpecificSynergy` events (festival, rainy, etc.).

**Headline:** Write failing unit tests in core describing the generic story-line model, compilation, resolution and journal/UI-adapter behaviour at parity with Main Street's current implementation — establishing the TDD baseline for the generic module.

## Problem statement

# Behaviour-preservation parity gate

**Headline:** Author the characterisation tests that pin today's behaviour (seeded storyline replay, the five shipped storylines, CSV option encodings and the adapter API results) **before** the refactor, so any semantic drift introduced by the move to core fails the suite.

## Problem statement

The most critical risk is subtle behaviour drift (RNG consumption order, option ordering, transcript text). A deterministic parity gate written against the current implementation turns the refactor into a safe, test-driven change: the tests are green now and must stay green after the move.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Seed-replay characterisation test: for a fixed seed the drawn storyline cards, presented options and resolution outcomes are recorded as a golden fixture and asserted equal, proving one seeded `rng()` draw per candidate selection at resolution time.
- A core-versus-Main-Street parity test asserts the generic core module produces identical compiled options and resolution results to today's Main Street modules for every choice card in `src/card-data.csv`, including legacy `hasChoices` cards and CSV `options` encodings.
- An adapter-output golden fixture captures the current journal rows, choice-clarity labels and story-update lines for the five shipped storylines (tax, health, economy, labour, restaurant); the adapters reproduce it byte-for-byte after the refactor.
- Behaviour preserved gate: the five shipped storylines and the CSV/card-pack authoring formats are validated end to end, CSV `options` encodings remain valid, and RNG seed replays produce identical results.
- Every test is green before the refactor begins (fixtures recorded in a work-item comment) and remains green after it; no assertion is weakened to accommodate the refactor.

## Minimal Implementation

- `core/tests/story-line/behaviour-parity.test.ts` — seeded replay + core-vs-Main-Street parity over the card data.
- `core/tests/story-line/validate-shipped.test.ts` — programmatic `validate-storylines` run.
- `core/tests/story-line/fixtures/` — golden replay and adapter-output fixtures.

## Key Files:

- `core/tests/story-line/validate-shipped.test.ts` — shipped-storyline validation

# Generic story-line module in core

**Headline:** Create a standalone, game-agnostic story-line module in Tableau-Card-Engine core: generic types, legacy/CSV option compilation, registry, resolution semantics, journal/pure helpers and a pluggable UI adapter — no Main Street imports and no Phaser dependency.

## Problem statement

The branching storyline mechanic lives in tce-main-street behind an extraction seam. Core needs a generic home with an inverted dependency on game state and presentation so any TCE game can ship branching card narratives.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Standalone generic storyline system in core: a new `core/src/story-line/` module with a barrel exporting the generic types, legacy `hasChoices` and CSV `options` compilation, the registered-option registry, resolution semantics (`apply`/`skip` effect policy, successor precedence, one seeded `rng()` draw per candidate selection), a pluggable UI adapter with a default implementation, and no Main-Street imports or Phaser dependency.
- Game coupling is inverted behind interfaces: a storyline engine adapter supplies state access (seeded `rng()` draw, effect application, activity-log append, chain-card sink) and a `StorylineUiAdapter` supplies names, choice-dialog labels, story-update lines and journal formatting; games override the default implementation without touching core logic.
- Resolution semantics preserved exactly: successor precedence (resolver → seeded candidate draw → legacy id), exactly one `rng()` draw per candidate selection at resolution time, terminal options consume no draw, `apply`/`skip` effect policy, and deterministic serial chain-card naming (`${base}-${maxSerial+1}`).
- Registry state is module-scoped and resettable for test isolation; no global state leaks between games or tests.
- Module-path alias resolves from both checkouts: `@story-line` added to `resolveCoreAliases`, `core/tsconfig.json`, the Main Street `tsconfig.json` and the scaffold template, with the existing alias tests updated and green.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean in core and all core story-line unit tests green (the tests authored in *Core story-line parity tests*).

## Minimal Implementation

- `types.ts` — `StorylineOption` (label, `successorId`, `successorIds`, `successorResolver`, `condition`, `effectPolicy`), `CompiledStoryline`, pending-choice state, engine/UI adapter interfaces.
- `compile.ts` — legacy `hasChoices` → two-option compilation, CSV `options` encoding parser, registry precedence, draw-time condition filtering.
- `resolve.ts` — effect policy, successor precedence, single seeded draw, chain-card push with deterministic serial naming.
- `journal.ts` + `ui-adapter.ts` — pure journal/choice-clarity/story-update helpers plus `defaultStorylineUiAdapter`.
- `index.ts` barrel + alias wiring in core and Main Street configs/scaffold.

## Key Files:

- `core/src/story-line/index.ts` — public barrel
- `core/src/story-line/types.ts` — generic types & adapter interfaces
- `core/src/story-line/compile.ts` — option compilation & registry
- `core/src/story-line/resolve.ts` — resolution & chain push
- `core/src/story-line/journal.ts` — journal helpers
- `core/src/story-line/ui-adapter.ts` — pluggable UI seam + default impl
- `core/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` — alias map
- `core/tsconfig.json` — core alias paths; `./tsconfig.json` — Main Street alias paths

## Dependencies

- Depends on *Core story-line parity tests* (edge wired) — tests drive the implementation.

## Deliverables

A usable, documented (JSDoc) generic story-line module in core with a pluggable UI seam, reachable from Main Street through a core alias.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: module location is `core/src/story-line/` with a new `@story-line` alias (the work item left the name TBD; the alias mechanism exists for exactly this and keeps the module out of `core-engine`).
- Assumption: the engine adapter is a narrow interface (rng draw, effect application, log append, chain sink) so Main Street can plug `MainStreetState` in F4 without core importing Main Street types.

# Main Street storyline adapters over core

**Headline:** Refactor `MainStreetStoryline.ts`, `MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts` and `MainStreetStorylineUi.ts` into thin adapters over the core story-line module, bump the core submodule pointer, and keep the entire existing Main Street storyline suite green and unchanged.

## Problem statement

Main Street's storyline modules are the seam's consumer side. They must delegate to core so the mechanic has a single implementation, while their exported API surface and player-visible behaviour stay identical.

## Acceptance Criteria

# Test-failure: heavy Monte-Carlo and deploy-build cases time out under load

## Summary

Several CPU-bound test cases in the `unit` project run close to (or beyond)
their per-test `testTimeout`, so the full suite turns red on a busy host even
though every assertion passes. They need the same explicit headroom that the
peer Monte-Carlo file already uses.

## Evidence

Observed during the MS-0MV8KSPFK006HTXG epic (F3I worktree, commit
`432e3b24`), full-suite runs on a loaded host (load average 10–33, 16 cores):

```
FAIL |unit| tests/main-street/competitive-monte-carlo.test.ts > AC1 — Deterministic head-to-head execution > should run ≥200 seeds in the batch harness
Error: Test timed out in 15000ms.
 ❯ tests/main-street/competitive-monte-carlo.test.ts:78:3

FAIL |unit| tests/main-street/favour-usage-metrics.test.ts > MonteCarloRunSummary — Community Favour usage counters > records integral, non-negative counters on every canonical greedy run
Error: Test timed out in 15000ms.
 ❯ tests/main-street/favour-usage-metrics.test.ts:22:3
```

Re-observing while validating this item (load average ~24) also surfaced the
same class of failure in the deploy build suite, which was blocking the
full-suite gate:

```
FAIL |unit| tests/deploy/pages-base-derivation.test.ts > production pages base derivation > derives /tce-main-street/ ... 
Error: Test timed out in 120000ms.
 ❯ tests/deploy/pages-base-derivation.test.ts:64:3
```

All Monte-Carlo files pass on a quiet run (dev HEAD, all 5833 assertions
green); the `≥200 seeds` case sits at ~8–12 s against a 15 s ceiling, and
`favour-usage-metrics` runs 200 seeds × 60 turns per case, so CPU contention
pushes either over the limit. The same contention also produced a
`[vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "onTaskUpdate"` unhandled error that made a
fully-passing run exit non-zero.

## Root cause

CPU-bound simulation loops sized at 200 seeds are inherently near the 15 s
unit default; full in-process production `vite build` cases measure 73–270 s
under load. Neither set declares adequate explicit per-test headroom.

## Precedent

`tests/main-street/monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts` already declares
`}, 120_000)` for its 200-seed cases, and `monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts`
runs 60 s+ per file. The failing files are the outliers.

## RPC teardown artefact (runner-level fix)

Even with every test green (5833 passed), Vitest exits non-zero when a
worker misses birpc's hard-coded 60 s `onTaskUpdate` RPC window under CPU
contention. The framework already ships the sanctioned mitigation:
`core/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` (CG-0MS9M5UJP005PWD3,
CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N) retries once on that exact signature and accepts a
second pure-transient result, while `shouldRetryOnce` refuses to mask any
genuine failure. `npm test` / `npm run test:unit` now invoke it (12-minute
per-attempt wall-clock bound, within the 1800 s per-command gate timeout).

## Scope note (deploy build files)

The deploy-build timeout fix was triaged as MS-0MVFSWC5Z000013W and is
delivered in this same commit: the two changes are mutually required for a
single green full-suite run (each worktree forked from `dev` only sees the
other's absence), so they land atomically. The item remains the tracked
record for the deploy-file failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every 200-seed Monte-Carlo case in `tests/main-street/competitive-monte-carlo.test.ts`
   that currently runs close to the limit declares an explicit per-test
   timeout of at least 60 s (matching the 120 s precedent in
   `monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts`).
2. Every 200-seed × 60-turn case in `tests/main-street/favour-usage-metrics.test.ts`
   declares an explicit per-test timeout of at least 60 s.
3. Every 200-seed case in `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts`
   declares the file's existing explicit 120 s per-test timeout (the
   `greedy Medium economy` case was the remaining outlier).
4. Every full-build/preview case in `tests/deploy/pages-base-derivation.test.ts`,
   `tests/deploy/vite-base-gating.test.ts` and `tests/deploy/preview-smoke.test.ts`
   declares an explicit per-test timeout of at least 300 s (shared
   `BUILD_TEST_TIMEOUT` constant; 600 s adopted after measuring ~270 s per
   build and ~238 s per preview-smoke case under load).
5. No assertions, fixture data, or simulation/build parameters change — the
   timeout is the only behavioural difference (beyond the explicit-limit
   declaration).
6. `npm run test` (and therefore `npm --silent test`) routes the `unit` +
   `unit-cli` projects through the framework's canonical
   `core/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`, so a fully-green run is not
   reported red by Vitest's transient birpc RPC teardown artefact
   (`[vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "onTaskUpdate"`). The runner's
   masking guard refuses to retry or accept any genuine test failure.
7. `npm run build` succeeds and the full suite passes via the test skill
   (`run_tests.py --scope full`).

## Key Files

- `tests/main-street/competitive-monte-carlo.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/favour-usage-metrics.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts`
- `tests/deploy/pages-base-derivation.test.ts`
- `tests/deploy/vite-base-gating.test.ts`
- `tests/deploy/preview-smoke.test.ts`
- `package.json`

# Test-failure: heavy production-build deploy tests time out at their 120 s per-test ceilings under load

## Summary

`tests/deploy/pages-base-derivation.test.ts` and (sibling risk)
`tests/deploy/vite-base-gating.test.ts` each run full in-process `vite build`
per test case. Under host/CI load a single build takes 73–120 s, so the
120 000 ms per-case ceiling was itself the failure: observed via the
MS-0MVFQ5ODR001R7U2 finish gate (load average ~24/16 cores) where
`pages-base-derivation.test.ts > derives /tce-main-street/ ...` timed out at
120 000 ms while its siblings took 91 s / 73 s and `vite-base-gating` passed
at 116 s — within 4 s of the same ceiling. All assertions pass; the failure
is headroom-only.

## Evidence

```
FAIL |unit| tests/deploy/pages-base-derivation.test.ts > production pages base derivation > derives /tce-main-street/ from package.json and gives the page a Main Street title
Error: Test timed out in 120000ms.
 ❯ tests/deploy/pages-base-derivation.test.ts:64:3
```

## Root cause

Real production builds are inherently 70–120 s under load; the explicit
120 s per-test timeout (`}, 120_000)`) leaves no margin — CPU contention
pushes a single case over the limit, and the run also surfaces
`[vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "onTaskUpdate"` (birpc 60 s default RPC
timeout) unhandled errors on fully-passing workers.

## Scope

# Main Street AI: cost-aware event-choice over the core presented option list

## Summary

Follow-up split out of the original Main Street epic `MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9` when the story-line engine was extracted into TCE core. The core epic (**CG-0MVI013DU000KEAB**) adds `cost`, `extraEffect`, and `conditionalSuccessors` to `StorylineOption` and cost-filtering to the draw-time presented snapshot.

Main Street owns the consumer AI policy and must be updated to score only the presented (cost-filtered) option list and account for cost/extra-effect deltas.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AI selection.** `decideEventChoice` (`src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts`) considers only options in the presented list; when a pending choice exists it reads `getPendingStorylineOptions(pending, state)`, otherwise `getStorylineOptions(event, state)`.
- **Cost-aware scoring.** Projected option value subtracts `cost.coins` and `cost.reputation` and adds `extraEffect` in addition to `effectPolicy` effects before comparing options.
- **AI harnesses.** Monte Carlo and regression harnesses run to completion without AI stalls or invalid selections; legacy binary-choice AI behaviour identical.
- **Determinism.** The policy stays RNG-free so seeded replays remain byte-identical.
- **Unit coverage.** Tests cover a cost-gated option being avoided and an extra-effect option that is only worthwhile once its delta is accounted for.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — `decideEventChoice` cost/extra-effect-aware scoring over the presented list.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — AI resolve path wiring.
- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — thin adapter over the core snapshot.

## Deliverables

- Updated AI policy.
- Regression/Monte Carlo harness tests green.
- Unit tests for AI policy with cost-gated and extra-effect options.

## Provenance

Refiled from `MS-0MURO1JZY002ZQG6`, a child of `MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9` (deleted after refile). It stays in Main Street because `decideEventChoice` and the AI harnesses are game-specific; core provides the snapshot.

## Dependencies

- **CG-0MVI013DU000KEAB** (core model, cost filtering, cost/extra effects, conditional successors).
