# Allow drag and drop from the hand

**Headline:** Hand-held businesses (and "possibly other cards") will not drag
to the play area. The producer reproduced this on a **local dev server** with
the tutorial off and actions remaining, in **Edge** — so this is a live defect
in the dev build, not a stale release: the hand-drag feature
(`MS-0MV76HVE4007AOO0`) is present in `dev` source but does not engage for the
player. Event cards are confirmed **click-only** by the producer. The job is to
reproduce on `dev`, root-cause, fix, and pin the behaviour with a regression
test that survives a scene refresh.

## Problem statement

> Seed report (producer): “Businesses, and possibly other cards, cannot be
> dragged and dropped from the hand to the play area.”

The market row drags to play in one gesture; the same gesture on a card that
has moved into the hand does nothing in the producer's local dev build. The
hand-drag implementation (`MS-0MV76HVE4007AOO0`, committed to `dev` as
`a447c0b7`) registers hand containers as `@ui/dragDrop` draggables and has
passing browser tests, so the failure is in a path those tests do not cover —
most plausibly a **refresh-cycle interaction**: `refreshMarket()` calls
`unregisterDragDraggables()` (which clears every registered draggable,
hand-origin ones included) and the hand is only re-registered when
`refreshPlayerHand()` runs afterwards in the same cycle. Any refresh path that
rebuilds or unregisters without re-rendering the hand leaves live hand cards
unregistered, so the pointer never starts a drag.

## Users

- **The player (human seat).** Single-player and the human seat in competitive
  play share the same hand input paths.

User stories:

- *As a player, I want to drag a business card from my hand onto an empty
  street slot so I can place it without the select-then-click two-step.*
- *As a player, I want the gesture I learn on the market row to keep working
  after a card has moved into my hand — including after I buy, sell or place
  something else.*
- *As a player, I want to know that event cards are played by clicking, so I do
  not read the missing drag as a bug.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Reproduction captured on `dev`.** A comment records the served checkout
   (`git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` + `git rev-parse --short HEAD`), browser
   (Edge, as reported), tutorial state (skipped/off) and actions remaining,
   plus the result of attempting a hand→street drag for a **business**,
   a **community-space** and an **upgrade** card. The reproduction must include
   a drag attempted both **immediately at turn start** and **after another
   action that triggers a scene refresh** (buy from market, sell, place, end
   turn), since the refresh path is the prime suspect.
2. **Root cause identified with evidence.** The failure is attributed to a
   specific code path (drag registration, refresh ordering, pointer hit-test,
   or browser input) and the attribution is backed by observable evidence —
   e.g. the hand container's `input`/draggable state and the
   `renderer.dragDropRegistered` membership at the moment of the failed drag —
   recorded on the work item. If the served checkout turns out to predate
   `a447c0b7`, that is recorded as the explanation instead, with the commit
   hashes proving it.
3. **Fix: hand drag works on `dev` for businesses, community-space and upgrade
   cards.** With the tutorial off and at least one action remaining, each of
   those families drags from the hand to a legal street target and resolves
   through the existing undoable commands (`playBusinessFromHandCommand` /
   `playUpgradeFromHandCommand`), with no action or coins spent on an illegal
   drop. Pure clicks still reach `onHandBusinessCardClick` /
   `onHandUpgradeCardClick` (drag-vs-click coexistence preserved).
4. **Refresh safety.** Drag registration survives every refresh path
   (`refreshAll`, `refreshAllExceptStreet`, and mid-turn partial refreshes):
   after each, hand cards remain draggable. The fix must not rely on a single
   render ordering; a guard (or an explicit re-registration step) makes the
   invariant hold by construction.
5. **Event cards stay click-only (producer-confirmed).** Hand-held event cards
   are not registered as draggables and keep the select-then-act `[Play]` /
   `[Discard]` flow; a test pins this so a future family-wide registration
   change cannot silently make them draggable.
6. **Regression tests.** Browser test coverage exercises a hand→street drag
   **after a scene refresh cycle** (the uncovered path), and a unit-level test
   covers the registration invariant directly. Assertions go through the
   scene's public interaction surface and resulting state — never source greps.
7. **Docs.** `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` hand-drag section states the
   supported hand families (business, community-space, upgrade) and that event
   cards are click-only; the refresh/registration invariant is documented in
   the code comment where it is enforced.
8. **Testing/validation.** The changed-scope test gate passes, and the new
   tests fail against the unfixed code (they genuinely reproduce the defect).
9. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
10. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Reuse the existing infrastructure:** the `@ui/dragDrop` manager, the street
  drop zones, the shared `dragHighlightRects` pool, `canPickUpHandCard` /
  `canDropHandCard`, and the undoable from-hand commands. No new engine state
  or action types.
- **Market-row drag behaviour is unchanged** (including the +50 % buy-and-play
  premium, which does not apply to hand-origin drags).
- **Do not regress the published build story:** `main`@`89118a84` (`v0.1.21`)
  still predates `a447c0b7`, so the published site also lacks the gesture. This
  item fixes the dev defect; shipping to `main` remains a producer-authorised
  ship-skill action, not part of this item.
- **Event cards are out of drag scope** — the producer has decided they stay
  click-only.
- **Browser matrix:** Edge (Chromium) is the reported browser; the headless
  Chromium browser tests are the executable proxy. Any Edge-only behaviour change
  must be called out explicitly.
- Investigation and code use **UK English**; all agent-initiated test runs go
  through the test skill.

## Existing state

- `dev` HEAD `19953f60`: hand containers are registered as draggables in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` (`renderCard` → both the upgrade and
  the business/community-space branches call `s.dragDropManager.registerDraggable`
  with `hitArea`, `canPickUp: canPickUpHandCard`, and the hand drop handlers).
  Drop-zone `canAccept` and the highlight resolver in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererDragDrop.ts` resolve the dragged id from the
  hand first, then the market.
- Refresh cycle (`src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` `refreshAll`):
  `refreshStreetGrid` → `refreshMarket` → `refreshIncidentQueue` →
  **`refreshPlayerHand`**. `refreshMarket` starts with
  `renderer.unregisterDragDraggables()` (`MainStreetRendererMarket.ts`), which
  unregisters **every** tracked draggable — market *and* hand — and clears
  `renderer.dragDropRegistered`. Only the subsequent `refreshPlayerHand` →
  `handView.setCards()` → `rebuildDisplay()` → `renderCard` re-registers hand
  cards. The invariant therefore depends on render ordering, not on the drag
  manager.
- `refreshAllExceptStreet` (`MainStreetRendererHud.ts`) has the same ordering:
  `refreshMarket` (unregister) → `refreshPlayerHand` (re-register).
- Existing tests: `tests/main-street/upgrade-hand-drag-drop.browser.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/drag.browser.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/hand-drag-drop.test.ts` — they drag shortly after boot;
  none exercises a drag after an action-triggered refresh.
- Docs (dev only): `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § "Hand-drag gesture:
  upgrades and business cards (MS-0MV76HVE4007AOO0)".
- `main`@`89118a84` (2026-10-16, `v0.1.21`) has no hand-drag registration at
  all, and `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` publishes `main` only.

## Desired change

- A reproduced, evidenced root cause for "hand cards will not drag" on `dev`.
- Hand→street drag that works for business, community-space and upgrade cards
  in the market phase, including after any refresh-triggering action.
- Drag registration that cannot be silently dropped by a later refresh (or a
  test that makes any regression immediate and loud).
- Event cards documented and tested as click-only.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` — the `unregisterDragDraggables()`
  call at the top of `refreshMarket` that clears hand-origin registrations.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererDragDrop.ts` — `unregisterDragDraggables`
  (registry scope: market-only vs all) and hand-origin resolution in
  `canAccept` / highlights.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — `refreshAll` /
  `refreshAllExceptStreet` ordering; the place to make the invariant explicit.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererLayout.ts` — `refreshPlayerHand` (re-registration
  point via `handView.setCards`).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — per-family `registerDraggable`
  calls and the click-vs-drag pointer handling.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerDragDrop.ts` — `canPickUpHandCard`,
  `canDropHandCard`, `onDragDropHandUpgrade`, `onDragDropHandBusiness`.
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-hand-drag-drop.browser.test.ts` /
  `tests/main-street/drag.browser.test.ts` — add the post-refresh drag case.
- `tests/main-street/hand-drag-drop.test.ts` — registration-invariant unit test.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — supported-family list + click-only events.

## Verification recipe (copy-paste)

```bash
# What is being served locally?
git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD && git rev-parse --short HEAD
git log --oneline -1 --grep='MS-0MV76HVE4007AOO0'

# Are hand draggables registered in the current tree?
grep -n 'registerDraggable' src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts
grep -n 'unregisterDragDraggables' src/scenes/MainStreetRenderer*.ts
```

Then, in Edge with the tutorial off and at least one action remaining: drag a
business card from the hand to an empty slot at turn start, then perform
another action (buy/sell/place) and repeat the drag. A dev-console probe of
`msRenderer.dragDropRegistered` / the hand container's `input.draggable`
immediately before the failed drag turns the symptom into the evidence AC2
requires.

## Related work

- `MS-0MV76HVE4007AOO0` — Allow drag and drop of upgrades from hand to card
  (completed, in review) — the implementation whose behaviour is failing.
- `MS-0MUUYGUVB009QOP6` — Drag-Drop Handlers: Pre-Drop Legality Audit
  (completed) — legality gate precedent.
- `MS-0MUUDWIXG009IB0W` — Reject illegal moves before animation and
  action-point deduction (completed) — the "no spend on illegal moves"
  invariant the hand drops must honour.
- `MS-0MV767QTO008JUDJ` — Clicking on a selected card in the hand deselects it
  (completed) — click-vs-drag coexistence precedent.
- `MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ` — MainStreetScene browser test timeouts are
  load-sensitive (open) — constrains how many extra browser scene boots the new
  regression test may add.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MV76HVE4007AOO0** – Allow drag and drop of upgrades from hand to card (completed)
- **MS-0MV767QTO008JUDJ** – Clicking on a selected card in the hand deselets it (completed)
- **MS-0MUUDWIXG009IB0W** – Reject illegal moves before animation and action-point deduction (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: allow, area, businesses, cannot, cards (+5 more)
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — matched: allow, area, businesses, cannot, cards (+5 more)
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: allow, area, businesses, cannot, cards (+5 more)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption A1:** the local dev server was serving a checkout containing
  `a447c0b7` (the producer's phrasing implies the current dev tree). If it was
  not, AC2 records the commit evidence and the item becomes a verification
  close-out instead of a fix. This is the single biggest swing in scope.
- **Assumption A2:** "play area" means the street tableau — the only placement
  surface for hand cards.
- **Risk R1:** the existing browser tests pass, so the defect is invisible to
  the current suite; a "fix" that does not add a post-refresh drag test could
  regress again. Mitigation: AC6 requires the new test to fail on the unfixed
  code.
- **Risk R2:** the registration invariant stays implicit (render ordering) and
  is re-broken by the next refresh change. Mitigation: AC4 requires an explicit
  guard, not just a reordered call.
- **Risk R3:** scope creep into a general drag-drop refactor of the core
  `@ui/dragDrop` module. Mitigation: changes stay in the game layer unless the
  evidence proves the manager at fault; a core change gets its own item.
- **Risk R4:** browser-suite load sensitivity (`MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ`) makes a
  new scene-booting test flaky. Mitigation: reuse the existing boot helper and
  keep added scene boots to one case.
- **Risk R5:** an Edge-only input difference (the reported browser) is not
  reproduced by headless Chromium tests. Mitigation: AC1 records the browser
  and AC2 requires the evidence probe in the real browser.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1: Which build was the failure observed on — the published site, a local
  `dev` server, or a packaged Electron build?** — Answer (producer, interactive
  reply): **local dev server**. That places the defect in the current `dev`
  tree rather than a stale published build, so the brief is scoped as a fix,
  not a close-out. Research: `dev` contains the hand-drag registration
  (`a447c0b7`); the prime suspect is the refresh cycle, where
  `refreshMarket()` calls `unregisterDragDraggables()` for every registered
  draggable and only `refreshPlayerHand()` re-registers hand cards.
- **Q2: Should hand-held event cards also be draggable, or stay
  click-only?** — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **no — click-only**.
  Applied as AC5 (no drag registration for events, select-then-act preserved,
  pinned by a test) and AC7 (documented). Matches the earlier recommendation.
- **Q3: If the failure also reproduces on the current `dev` build, what were
  the exact steps?** — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **tutorial off,
  actions remaining, Edge browser**. Applied in AC1 (reproduction context and
  browser) and AC3 (tutorial off, at least one action remaining).
- **Q4: Which branch/commit was the local dev server serving when the drag
  failed?** — **OPEN QUESTION.** Decides between "fix a dev defect" (expected)
  and "verify and close as already-working". Evidence can be recovered during
  AC1 by reading the served checkout's `HEAD`; if the producer can confirm
  "latest `dev`", AC1 is satisfied faster. **Recommended:** latest `dev`
  (`19953f60` or later).

- **Q5: Who captures the Edge reproduction — the producer manually, or the agent via headless Chromium browser tests?** — Decision (plan agent): agent-first via the headless Chromium proxy, escalating to the producer only if it does not reproduce; the repro child's ACs record the browser used and parent risk R5 requires any Edge-only difference to be called out explicitly. Rationale: the browser suite is the executable proxy and a producer round-trip is expensive. **OPEN for producer confirmation** only if the producer insists on capturing Edge evidence themselves — then the repro child gains a producer action.
- **Q6: Should the docs update be its own child item?** — Decision (plan agent): no — folded into the fix child, because the docs describe the invariant the fix establishes; keeping them together makes that child a complete vertical slice (code + tests + docs, parent AC7/AC9).
- **Q4 update (plan session):** still OPEN at planning time; it becomes resolvable by the repro child's served-checkout evidence (AC1). If the served checkout predates `a447c0b7`, the plan collapses to a verification close-out and children 2–3 are re-planned (see Plan block, scope note).

## Assumptions carried into the brief

- Event cards stay click-only (confirmed by the producer).
- The published build's missing gesture is a separate, already-known release
  gap and is not reopened here.
- "Play area" means the street tableau.


## Plan (decomposition)

Planned in session `herdr-1792708350-1638779-5737` (2026-10-22). The bug splits into three child items in **test-first, dependency order**:

| # | Child (ID) | Type | Parent ACs covered |
|---|------------|------|--------------------|
| 1 | Reproduce hand-drag failure with registration evidence (`MS-0MVK4E4KU002KU23`) | task | AC1, AC2 |
| 2 | Add regression tests for post-refresh hand drags (`MS-0MVK4E56S0059JPY`) | task | AC5, AC6, AC8 (red-before-fix evidence) |
| 3 | Fix hand-drag registration invariant and update docs (`MS-0MVK4E5M00021XEY`) | bug | AC3, AC4, AC7, AC9 |

Dependency edges: **2 → 1** (the evidence names the failing refresh path and the probe API the tests target) and **3 → 2** (tests are written and shown red before the fix lands). AC10 (full project suite) needs no child: it is enforced by the dev-push gate.

Vertical-slice check: each child is self-contained and end-to-end in its own role — 1 is an investigation slice (regression evidence deliverable), 2 is a test slice (red), 3 is the code+docs slice (green). There is no horizontal "layer" phase. Between phases, re-read the next child's description and update it with the previous child's findings.

Scope note (AC2 contingency): if child 1 shows the served checkout predates `a447c0b7`, the tree collapses — child 1 closes as a verification close-out and children 2–3 are re-planned; never implement a fix for a defect that does not exist on the checked-out code.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-22 (plan session `herdr-1792708350-1638779-5737`):
  - Effort/risk pre-check → `decision: plan` (effort Small, risk Medium; the risk is above the `Low` skip threshold).
  - Plan-approval gate → `request_approval: false` (approval pauses apply only to Extra Large effort **and** High/Severe risk).
  - Created 3 child items (test-first order) and wired dependency edges 2→1, 3→2.
  - No existing content rewritten — the intake description, ACs and Appendix are preserved; only the Plan block and Appendix entries above were added.

# Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player, when a competitive game against the AI ends (e.g. I win
because the AI goes bankrupt) and I click **[ Play Again ]**, the new match must
start completely fresh and must not be decided on its opening day: no seat
carries over any wallet, elimination flag, hand, staff or score from the
finished run, and the AI cannot be bankrupt on the first turn of the new game.

# Reported behaviour (repro)

1. Play a competitive game (human vs AI).
2. Win: the AI seat goes bankrupt and the game-over overlay appears.
3. Click **[ Play Again ]** and start a new game.
4. The AI is bankrupt again — reported as "went bankrupt in the first turn".
   The reporter's hypothesis: "their stats were not reset".

# Root cause (investigation)

The reporter's hypothesis was **wrong about the mechanism**, but the symptom is
real and reproducible.

- **The Play Again / New Game path is clean.** `createCompetitiveState()` seeds
  every `PlayerRecord` from the difficulty preset (Medium: 600 coins / 300 rep,
  `eliminated` unset, empty hand/staff, score 0). Verified by simulation: new
  games after a finished run always started with fresh seats.
- **The real defect is an opening-day elimination.** Competitive AI seats are
  driven by the single-player `Greedy` / `BankingGreedy` strategies, which spend
  freely down to the last coin — e.g. hiring 400 of the 600 starting coins on
  turn 1. The shared closing then applies the day's incident (a flat `-200`
  Protest, `-500` General Strike, or an accepted dual-choice option) to a wallet
  that can no longer absorb it, so the seat goes negative and is **eliminated on
  turn 1**. With one AI opponent that immediately ends the match
  (`last_standing` / bankruptcy), so the player sees "the AI went bankrupt in
  the first turn" right after Play Again. Measured on 80 seeds per
  strategy/difficulty combination, 1–5 % of *first-ever* games were decided on
  turn 1 this way (two reproduced failure seeds are pinned in the regression
  test as `dayone-12` and `dayone-42`).

# Scope

In scope:

- Competitive opening-day solvency (no seat can be bankrupted on turn 1).
- AI seat liquidity: AI seats keep a difficulty-gated reserve instead of
  spending their last coins.
- Regression coverage for both, plus a guard that a new game after a finished
  run starts from fresh seats.
- Game rules documentation.

Out of scope:

- AI strategy strength / balance tuning beyond the liquidity floor.
- Single-player loss conditions (unchanged: bankruptcy can still end a
  single-player game on turn 1).
- Changing incident card values or the shared incident deck.

# Acceptance criteria

1. **Fresh seats on a new competitive game.** Creating a competitive game after
   a finished one yields every `PlayerRecord` at the preset's starting
   coins/reputation with `eliminated` unset, empty hand/staff, score 0 and no
   failure badges. *Metric: automated test after a played run whose AI seat is
   left bankrupt/eliminated.*
2. **The opening day cannot be decided by debt.** A competitive seat that would
   end turn 1 with negative coins has its debt written off to 0 (logged as
   `First-day grace: …`) and is not eliminated; no bankruptcy game-over is
   declared on turn 1. *Metric: unit test of `applyFirstSharedDaySolvencyGrace`
   plus the two reproduced day-1 failure seeds (`dayone-12`, `dayone-42`) still
   running at turn 2 with both seats solvent.*
3. **Bankruptcy elimination is unchanged from turn 2.** A negative seat from
   turn 2 onwards still fails `checkCompetitiveSeatFailure` and is eliminated
   exactly as before. *Metric: unit test.*
4. **AI seats keep a liquidity reserve.** `competitiveAiReserveCoins` is
   difficulty-gated (Easy 50 %, Medium 35 %, Hard 25 % of the preset's starting
   coins); a bound AI seat sees only its spendable balance, restores exactly the
   withheld reserve (never charged), and an AI MarketPhase never takes the seat
   below its reserve. *Metric: automated tests + a full AI MarketPhase across
   several seeds.*
5. **Single-player unchanged.** The grace is inert without a `players[]` roster
   and single-player bankruptcy still applies on any turn. *Metric: unit test
   plus the existing suite.*

# Key Files

- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngine.ts`
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`
- `tests/main-street/competitive-play-again-reset.test.ts`

# Assumptions (documented for the producer)

- Because incidents are drawn from the shared deck and their size is outside a
  seat's control, a liquidity reserve alone cannot guarantee the AI will not be
  bankrupted on the opening day (`-500` General Strike vs a 600-coin purse), so
  a **symmetric turn-1 solvency grace** is applied to every competitive seat.
  It mirrors the pre-existing turn-1 grace for reputation collapse, and it
  changes competitive play only; single-player keeps its rules.
- The reserve is applied in the interactive AI driver only. Headless harnesses,
  Monte Carlo balance runs and the human seat are unaffected, so the balance
  baseline gate is untouched by design.

## Impact

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `<suite exited 1>: npm --silent test` passes when run against the latest `dev`.
2. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

# Make `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` waits load-tolerant

## Headline

Two `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` waits use fixed budgets that are shorter than
the production deferral caps they are racing, so the browser gate fails under host
CPU contention even though the scene behaves correctly.

## Problem statement

`tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` contains two assertions that
poll for an animation-gated outcome with a fixed timeout:

| Test | Wait | Label | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allows pressing Enter to end the turn when legal` | `scene.state.turn > beforeTurn` | `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` | 15 000 ms |
| `only materializes purchased cards at destination after transfer animation completes` | card present in `state.hand` | `business bought to hand` | 6 000 ms |

Both waits race Phaser `requestAnimationFrame`-driven tweens and the scene's own
bounded deferrals. Under CPU saturation (load average 20–58 observed from
concurrent agent suites across repositories) rAF callbacks are starved, the
animations stretch well past their nominal duration, and the poll exhausts its
budget before the scene reaches the gated state. The production code then
finishes correctly — the test has already thrown.

The first wait is the sharper defect: the end-of-turn income deferral in
`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` uses a **16 000 ms** safety cap
before it forces the day start. The test waits **15 000 ms** — one second *less*
than the cap the code is explicitly allowed to consume. Under starvation the
test can therefore fail while the scene is still within its own documented,
bounded budget.

## Users

- **Agent-implementer** running the browser gate via `/skill:test` or an
  implement-gate step: needs a deterministic gate; a red browser suite blocks
  the build → test → commit order and burns whole sessions on retries.
- **Human maintainer** reviewing a failing gate: needs to trust that a red
  browser test means a real defect, not host weather.
- **Release engineer** running the dev-push gate: needs the full suite green on
  a shared, often-loaded build host.

Example user stories:

> As an agent running the browser gate on a busy host, I want waits to be
> derived from the scene's own bounded timing constants, so that a pass does not
> depend on how many sibling suites are running.

> As a maintainer reading a red browser test, I want failures to mean behavioural
> regressions only, so that I do not have to triage false positives from load.

## Existing state

- The two failure signatures are already recorded as completed test-failure
  items: MS-0MVI510GD0061C3M and MS-0MVKYFC7O009LUJV (both `completed`), each
  with the same `Timed out waiting for turn to advance after end-of-turn
  presentation after 15000ms` signature. Repeat occurrences mean the per-run
  triage closed the symptom without fixing the cause.
- The scene runs a phased income choreography (`src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts`,
  constants in `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts`) with nominal phase gaps
  of 2 200 ms, and multiple bounded deferral paths that poll a 16 000 ms cap
  (`MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` lines ~432, ~616, ~782;
  `MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` `incomeCollectionCapMs` default
  `16_000`).
- Market→hand and hand→board transfer durations are bounded by
  `DRAG_TRANSFER_DURATION_MIN_MS` / `DRAG_TRANSFER_DURATION_MAX_MS`
  (`250`–`1 500` ms) in `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts`.
- Existing precedent for load-tolerant budgets is a **hard-coded generous
  margin**, not a derivation: `tests/main-street/incident-reveal.browser.test.ts`
  uses `4_000 + 16_000`, and `tests/main-street/income-collection.browser.test.ts`
  uses `PHASED_SHOW_MS + 16000`, both with comments explaining CPU contention.
- `waitForCondition` is copied verbatim into **49 test files**; there is no
  shared helper (`core/tests/helpers/` contains only `waitForScene.ts`,
  `phaserCanvasPool.ts`, `MockFactory.ts`, `FakeReplayAdapter.ts`).
- The browser Vitest project has `testTimeout: 60_000`, `fileParallelism: false`,
  `sequence.concurrent: false` (`vite.config.ts`).
- The retry runner (`core/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`) retries only on the
  three known *transient* signatures (worker RPC timeout, browser socket drop,
  true hang). A `waitForCondition` timeout is a **genuine** test failure to that
  runner, so it is not retried — one load spike fails the gate outright.
- Reduced motion is a persisted user preference (`_reducedMotion` in
  `core/src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`, read via `getReducedMotion(localStorage)`), and
  the animators honour it (`src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorBoard.ts`,
  `MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts`, `MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts`,
  `MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts`). Reduced motion skips flights but
  *keeps* the incident hold and the advance gating.

## Desired change

Two of the three options in the originating description are viable; the third is
not acceptable as the sole remedy.

**Proposed (recommended): derive the waits from the scene's own bounded caps,
via one shared, load-tolerant wait helper.**

1. Publish the deferral caps the tests race as named exported constants
   (e.g. an exported end-of-turn income-collection cap from the turn controller /
   animator timing module, and the transfer-duration bounds already exported from
   `MainStreetConstants.ts`), so a test can import the number rather than guess.
2. Add a shared browser-test helper (alongside `core/tests/helpers/waitForScene.ts`)
   that exposes `waitForCondition` with a **nominal budget + starvation margin**
   model: budget = `nominalCapMs * starvationFactor + fixedFloorMs`, or simply
   `cap + margin`, with the invariant enforced that the budget is never shorter
   than the production cap it races.
3. Use it in the two failing waits so both are ≥ the cap they can legitimately
   consume (the Enter wait must exceed the 16 000 ms income-collection cap; the
   transfer wait must exceed the transfer-duration cap plus scheduling slack).
4. Assert the invariant so the defect cannot silently return: a unit test (or a
   guard test over the test file) that fails if a browser-test budget constant is
   smaller than the production cap it is documented as racing.

**Rejected: accept as a known flake (option c).** The retry runner does not retry
`waitForCondition` timeouts, so "accept and document the retry expectation" would
leave the gate red with no automated recovery. Documenting a manual re-run
expectation also contradicts the project's "all tests must pass before a push to
`dev`" policy.

**Rejected as the sole remedy: force reduced motion (option b).** Reduced motion
skips the flight animations but keeps the advance gating, so it would change what
the Enter test exercises: the deferred income-collection window
(CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q) is precisely the path that the test currently covers. Using
it would mask the real deferral path from coverage. It stays available as a
*complement* in tests that are not about animation pacing.

**Non-goal (recorded, not scoped here):** consolidating all 49 copies of
`waitForCondition` onto the new shared helper. That is a large mechanical
refactor; this item leaves the shared helper in place and adopts it in the two
load-sensitive waits, so the 49-copy duplication can be retired separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` wait in
      `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` is derived from an
      exported end-of-turn income-collection deferral cap (instead of the bare
      `15_000` literal), and its budget is strictly greater than that cap so a
      load-stretched scene can never outlive the poll.
- [x] The `business bought to hand` wait in the same file is derived from the
      exported card-transfer duration bounds (plus documented scheduling slack),
      not a bare `6_000` literal.
- [x] A shared, load-tolerant `waitForCondition` helper is added under
      `core/tests/helpers/` (sibling to `waitForScene.ts`), with a documented
      `nominal cap + starvation margin` budget model, and both fixed waits use it.
- [x] A regression guard fails the build if any browser-test wait budget is
      smaller than the production cap it is documented as racing (so the
      15 000 ms-vs-16 000 ms mismatch cannot be reintroduced); the guard imports
      the constants rather than restating literals.
- [x] Reliability proven, not assumed: at least 20 consecutive local runs of
      `npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts`
      pass, including at least one run under imposed CPU load.
- [x] At least one unit test covers the new helper's budget derivation
      (`nominal`, `starvationFactor`, `floor`), and the guard test above is thus
      part of the suite.
- [x] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [x] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No behavioural change to production pacing. The fix must not shorten or remove
  the income choreography, the incident hold, or the deferral caps — those are
  user-visible features (CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ, CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q) and changing
  them to satisfy a test would invert the dependency.
- Browser-project `testTimeout` is `60_000`; any derived budget must leave
  headroom for boot plus teardown within that hook.
- `waitForCondition` copies live in 49 test files; the new helper must not force
  a wholesale edit of them in this item.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` and the animator timing module are the
  single sources of truth for the durations; the tests must consume them, not
  duplicate them.
- Writes to `core/` follow the engine-sync workflow (`npm run engine:sync` /
  `engine:verify`); confirm whether the shared helper belongs in the core
  checkout or the game repository before implementing.
- Vitest browser tests run serially; the guard test must stay cheap.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` — Replace the two
  hard-coded `15_000` / `6_000` budgets with values derived from exported caps.
- `core/tests/helpers/waitForCondition.ts` — New shared load-tolerant poll
  helper (nominal cap + starvation margin), sibling to `waitForScene.ts`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts` — Export the end-of-turn
  income-collection deferral cap (`16_000`) as a named constant instead of a
  repeated inline literal.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — Consume the new named cap
  in the three `startAt = s.time.now + 16_000` deferral sites.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` — Default
  `incomeCollectionCapMs` to the new named constant.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — Already exports the transfer bounds;
  confirm they are the values the test should race.
- `tests/main-street/browser-wait-budget-guard.test.ts` — New guard asserting
  every documented test budget exceeds the production cap it races.
- `tests/tooling/` or `core/tests/` — Unit test for the helper's budget
  derivation (`nominal`, `starvationFactor`, `floor`).
- `docs/dev/` (testing guidance) — Document the load-tolerant wait model.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the two failures are purely starvation-driven and there is no
  latent behavioural race. Evidence: both pass 20/20 on a quiet host
  (`51–69 s`), and the 15 000 ms budget sits below the 16 000 ms production cap.
  A long-run soak under artificial load is the confirmation step, not a
  precondition.
- **Risk:** deriving nowhere near enough headroom still flakes on a 90 s+ stall.
  Mitigation: the helper's budget is `cap + margin` with the invariant asserted,
  and the 60 s `testTimeout` stays the outer bound so a genuine hang still
  surfaces as a hang, not a false pass.
- **Risk:** a generous budget slows the suite when a test legitimately fails
  (failure now costs the full budget). Mitigation: keep budgets derived and
  minimal-but-sufficient; the suite is serial and already gated at 60 s.
- **Risk:** lifting the cap constant into a shared module creates a game→engine
  dependency churn. Mitigation: confirm placement in `core/` vs the game repo
  first; if the helper belongs in `core/`, follow `engine:sync`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** the attractor here is "unify all 49 `waitForCondition`
  copies" and "make every wait in every browser test derived". Both are
  explicitly out of scope; record them as linked work items rather than
  expanding this one.
- **Risk:** the guard test could become a brittle source-of-truth duplicate
  (re-listing numbers). Mitigation: the guard must import the constants, not
  restate literals.

## Related work

- MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ — this item (discovered during the implement gate for
  MS-0MVJNFESC005QJ41).
- MS-0MVI510GD0061C3M — `[test-failure] … allows pressing Enter to end the turn
  when legal` (completed): same 15 000 ms signature, under heavy host load.
- MS-0MVKYFC7O009LUJV — `[test-failure] … allows pressing Enter to end the turn
  when legal` (completed): same signature, load average ~26.
- MS-0MVIKAVS2006WN9K — `[test-failure] … shows the full tooltip when hovering a
  business card in the hand (AC2)` (completed): same file, same contention class.
- MS-0MV8MC3MX008Z4ZZ — `[test-failure] … routes mapped SFX keys to tf-backed
  adapter when tf module is provided` (completed): another `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts`
  timeout-class failure; surfaced by find-related during intake.
- MS-0MV2DORIC001Y9XZ — `[test-failure] income-collection.browser.test.ts …
  animateIncomePhases` (completed): the +16 s margin precedent.
- MS-0MUO7CPH3003TXFI — `Reduce time upcoming event is shown` (completed): the
  incident reveal hold the Enter wait races.
- MS-0MV8LHN0W0017XU1 — `Reputation bonuses should have no delay between
  businesses` (completed): recent income-choreography pacing change.
- MS-0MUYFX7Q2004JQ5R — shared end-of-turn closing presentation primitive that
  carries `incomeCollectionCapMs`.
- `core/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` — the retry runner that does *not*
  retry `waitForCondition` timeouts (why option (c) is not viable).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Which remediation should the item implement — (a) derive the two waits from
  the animator's bounded caps via a shared load-tolerant helper, (b) force
  reduced motion in these tests, or (c) document the flake and accept a retry
  expectation?
  — Answer (producer): **(a)** — derive the waits from the animator's bounded
  caps via a shared load-tolerant helper. Source: interactive reply (intake
  interview round 1). Research: the 15 000 ms wait is one second shorter than
  the 16 000 ms production deferral cap it races (`MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`
  `startAt = s.time.now + 16_000`; `MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts`
  `incomeCollectionCapMs` default `16_000`), so this is a real mismatch rather
  than a taste preference; (b) removes the deferred-income path from coverage
  and (c) cannot work because `core/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` does not
  retry `waitForCondition` timeouts. Follow-up (unanswered, non-blocking):
  helper placement — draft assumes `core/tests/helpers/` next to
  `waitForScene.ts`, consistent with the existing `@core-tests/helpers` import
  pattern.

## Related work (automated report)

Gathered via `/skill:find-related` (report persisted at
`.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ.md`).

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVI510GD0061C3M** – [test-failure] MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts >
  MainStreetScene browser tests > allows pressing Enter to end the turn when
  legal — failing test (completed)
- **MS-0MVKYFC7O009LUJV** – [test-failure] MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts >
  allows pressing Enter to end the turn when legal — failing test (completed)
- **MS-0MV8MC3MX008Z4ZZ** – [test-failure] MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts >
  MainStreetScene browser tests > routes mapped SFX keys to tf-backed adapter
  when tf module is provided — failing test (completed)

### Related repository files
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — engine developer guide; testing/pacing context.
- `core/AGENTS.md` — engine agent instructions; relevant to whether the shared
  helper belongs in the core checkout.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — documents reduced motion, deferral pacing and
  presentation behaviour that these waits must respect.

## Completion evidence (2026-10-24)

All six children are implemented, tested, committed and pushed to `dev` (each
`in_review`); see the per-child evidence comments for full detail.

| Child | Commit(s) on dev | What landed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — shared helper | `c3315267` (core) + game pointer/pin bump (delivered in `0f7f1716`) | `core/tests/helpers/waitForCondition.ts` + unit tests (TDD), core unit suite (3184 tests) + core build green, pushed to core `dev` |
| 2 — cap constant | `18ece840` | `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS = 16_000` exported, three `s.time.now + 16_000` deferral sites + `incomeCollectionCapMs` default consumed it, unit pins the four consumers |
| 3 — guard | `ef48dfeb` | `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts` (node unit): derives budgets from imported caps, budget > cap invariant, sub-cap option sets throw, budget + 20 s boot ≤ 60 s hook; `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` `unit` type |
| 4 — adoption | `4093c711` | Enter wait + `business bought to hand` + `first business bought to hand` use the shared helper with `capMs`; legacy local helper marked `@deprecated`; guard's source scan covers the documented labels |
| 5 — docs | `4689abf6` | `docs/dev/testing.md`: the cap+margin model, the `capMs`/`floorMs` API, the strict-greater invariant, the 60 s headroom rule, why retries are not a substitute, exact guard + soak commands, and the measured soak envelope |
| 6 — soak | `9f2c6185` | `scripts/soak-browser-waits.sh`, `soak`/`soak-load` profiles, harness unit tests; **20/20 quiet passes**, **2 under-load passes** (8 burners, load 23.6) — full evidence table on the child |
| 7 — pin consistency fix | `1660e961` | Aligned `configs/engine-pin.json` to the committed core gitlink (d907af9f); full suite green at HEAD |

**AC mapping:** 1→2/4, 2→4, 3→1, 4→3(+6), 5→6, 6→1, 7→5, 8→every child's finish gate.

**Reliability evidence (AC5):** quiet soak 20/20 (peak load 15.3, 58-107 s/run);
under imposed CPU load two consecutive full passes (8 burners, peak 23.6), and
the ≥nproc-burner ceiling measured at ~2× oversubscription is documented with
the exact numbers, not accepted as a flake — follow-ups `MS-0MVMKEU2000639TG`
(hook ceiling) and `MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O` (engine doc-heading contract).

**Non-goals honoured:** none of the 49 legacy `waitForCondition` copies were
migrated; no production pacing constant changed (single exception: constant
extraction only); `hand card selected for placement` wait untouched.

# Intake Brief — `unit-cli` project is silently skipped by `npm test`

## Problem statement

`npm test` (the retry runner invoking `vitest run --project unit --project unit-cli`)
regularly executes only the `unit` project: none of the five serialized CLI files in
`CLI_TEST_FILES` are collected, no `|unit-cli|` lines are reported, and the run is still
green. The Playwright-driven `storyline-graph-svg` render/doc-drift guard and the four
storyline/harness CLI suites therefore run in some full-suite runs and not in others, so a
green gate does not mean everything ran.

## Users

- **Implementer / agent** running the changed-scope or full-suite gate before committing —
  needs "green" to mean "every non-browser test file ran".
- **Reviewer / auditor** reading a cached gate result (`.worklog/cache/*/stdout.txt`) —
  needs the run's coverage to be reproducible for a given commit.
- **Release engineer** promoting `dev` → `main` — needs the gate evidence to be trustworthy.

### User stories

- As an implementer, when the gate reports green I want evidence that every configured
  project contributed its files, so a CLI-test regression cannot slip through unnoticed.
- As an auditor, I want a green cached run to be reproducible — the same commit must not
  sometimes exercise 375 files and sometimes 380.

## Evidence (verified during intake, 2026-10-23)

- `HEAD` = `582ab9e5` holds **380** non-browser `*.test.ts` files; `CLI_TEST_FILES` in
  `vite.config.ts` holds **5**.
- The most recent cached full run (`5cb02674`, 2026-10-23 11:09Z, exit 0) reports
  `Test Files 375 passed (375)` and contains **zero** occurrences of any of the five CLI
  file names — exactly the 5 CLI files are missing and `unit-cli` contributed nothing.
  Same shape in `6edb5947` (371), `6773e550` (370), `abb42afc` (365), `091fb66e` (373).
- **Arg forwarding is not the cause.** The runner's own diagnostic in a skipping run reads
  `[vitest-runner] attempts=2 status=0 outcome=accepted-transient args="--project unit --project unit-cli"`;
  both retry attempts skipped the project identically, so it is not a transient-teardown
  artefact and not a lost flag.
- **Not a persistent config regression.** The identical main checkout ran `unit-cli`
  successfully at 2026-10-22 16:49Z (`7b5c9894`, five `|unit-cli|` lines) between two runs
  that did not (21:10Z `6edb5947`, 21:53Z `6773e550`). Every run reports
  `RUN v3.2.7 /home/rgardler/projects/tce-main-street`.
- **Block structure suggests state, not source:** every run up to 2026-10-18 01:21Z shows
  `|unit-cli|`; runs from 2026-10-19 21:21Z on mostly do not — yet no commit touched
  `vite.config.ts` or `package.json` between `a2a25864` (2026-10-18 01:17Z) and
  `866294b5` (2026-10-20 01:02Z).
- The existing guard `tests/main-street/vitest-cli-project-isolation.test.ts` asserts the
  **declared** config shape (project names, `include`/`exclude`, serialization flags) but
  not the **run-time project selection**, which is precisely why it stays green while the
  project is skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Root cause identified and fixed at the cause — the work item records which hypothesis
   (H1 zero-file collection, H2 project filtered out, H3 stale environment state, or another)
   was confirmed, with the evidence that confirmed it; if the cause proves to be a Vitest
   defect, it is documented in the item as an upstream issue rather than papered over.
2. `npm test` deterministically executes all five `CLI_TEST_FILES` in a **single** Vitest
   invocation (both `--project` flags retained — no additional invocation stage): proof is a
   full-suite run containing `|unit-cli|` lines for every one of them (or an equivalent
   machine-checkable record, e.g. JSON-reporter entries with `projectName: unit-cli`), and the
   item records the measured before/after suite duration showing no meaningful increase.
3. A run in which a configured project contributes **zero** test files fails loudly instead
   of reporting green, naming the empty project and its expected files.
4. A regression test pins the run-time selection for the `npm test` argument set: `unit` and
   `unit-cli` are both resolved, every non-browser `tests/**/*.test.ts` file is claimed by
   exactly one project, and the five CLI files are claimed only by `unit-cli` (fast static
   check that runs in the `unit` project).
5. `docs/dev/testing.md` documents the deterministic invocation, the zero-file guard and the
   intermittent-skip symptom, including what a green full-suite run must contain.
6. Full project test suite passes with the changes (`/skill:test`).

## Constraints

- **Fix the quirk, do not route around it** (producer decision, 2026-10-23): keep the single
  `vitest run --project unit --project unit-cli` invocation and repair the project-selection
  behaviour at its cause. Adding a second invocation stage is acceptable only if the root
  cause proves unfixable — and the resulting wall-clock cost must then be measured and
  reported back to the producer.
- **Preserve MS-0MV5PNIPO00940KG isolation.** The five CLI files must not return to the
  parallel `unit` pool; they flake under file-level parallelism (spurious
  `expected 1 to be +0`).
- **Repository boundary.** `core/` is the engine submodule: `core/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`
  and `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` belong to the engine repo. Prefer a fix that
  lives in this repo (`package.json` script, `vite.config.ts`, a local wrapper, tests).
  If an engine-side change proves necessary, **raise it as a separate item in
  `../ContextHub`** (producer instruction, 2026-10-23) rather than bundling it here; an
  engine change also needs its own `engine:sync`/pin discipline. Note for the implementer:
  `./core` resolves to `../Tableau-Card-Engine`, while `../ContextHub` is the Worklog (`wl`)
  tooling repo — confirm the target repository at that point if the distinction matters.
- **`vite.config.ts` is auto-generated** from `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, and that
  template does **not** carry `CLI_TEST_FILES`/`unit-cli`. Keep local edits surgical and
  documented so a future re-scaffold does not silently drop them (precedent:
  MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY applied a surgical sync for the same reason).
- Keep `vitest-run-with-retry.ts` semantics intact: retry-once on transient contention
  signatures, never retry a hang, never mask a genuine failure.
- Do not weaken the masking guard in order to make the gate green.

## Existing state

- `package.json`: `test` and `test:unit` both run
  `tsx core/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts --timeout-ms 720000 --project unit --project unit-cli`.
- `vite.config.ts` declares three projects: `unit` (parallel, `maxWorkers: 4`,
  `exclude: ['tests/**/*.browser.test.ts', ...CLI_TEST_FILES]`), `unit-cli`
  (`include: CLI_TEST_FILES`, `fileParallelism: false`,
  `sequence: { concurrent: false, groupOrder: 1 }`, 180 s timeout) and `browser`.
- Vitest 3.2.7. In this version a project is dropped silently in exactly two places: it
  throws `VitestFilteredOutProjectError` when no potential project name matches the
  `--project` filter, and it is kept but contributes no specs when its `include` matches
  nothing — neither produces a failure on its own.
- Two guards exist: `tests/main-street/vitest-cli-project-isolation.test.ts` (config shape)
  and `tests/main-street/testing-docs-projects.test.ts` (docs/config drift).

## Desired change

**Route (producer decision, 2026-10-23): diagnose and fix the quirk itself.** Keep the single
`vitest run --project unit --project unit-cli` invocation; do not add a second invocation
stage unless the root cause proves unfixable, and if it does, measure and report the added
wall-clock cost.

Diagnose, in this order (cheapest discriminating evidence first):

- **H1 — zero-file collection.** The `unit-cli` project initialises but its `include` matches
  nothing (root / `include` resolution inside an `extends: true` project), and Vitest reports
  green for a project that contributed no files.
- **H2 — project filtered out.** `VitestFilteredOutProjectError` drops the project because
  the effective `--project` name filter does not match the declared name
  (`matchesProjectFilter` consults `config.project || cliOptions.project`).
- **H3 — stale environment state.** A cached Vite/Vitest config or dependency artefact (or
  `core` submodule state, which several tests mutate via `engine:sync`) makes project
  resolution vary between runs of the same commit.

First diagnostic step (agent-initiated runs must go through `/skill:test`): capture one
full-suite run with `--reporter=json` and diff the project names present against the three
projects declared in `vite.config.ts`; `vitest list --project unit --project unit-cli` from a
clean `node_modules/.vite` state is the follow-up probe. Record which of H1–H3 the evidence
supports in the work item before changing code.

Then fix at the cause. Candidate remedies, to be chosen by the evidence:

- explicit `root` on the `unit-cli` project (removes dependence on inherited root
  resolution), or a project definition that does not rely on `extends: true` inheriting the
  root `test` block;
- an unambiguous project-name filter (e.g. non-overlapping names, or a documented
  `--project` form) if the filter matching is the culprit;
- clearing/defeating the stale cache path if H3 is confirmed (and documenting the cache
  invalidation requirement in `docs/dev/testing.md`).

Regardless of the remedy, land AC3 (loud zero-file failure) and AC4 (run-time selection +
full file-coverage guard) so a future silent skip fails the gate instead of passing it.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `package.json` — `test` / `test:unit` scripts; possibly split into per-project invocations
- `vite.config.ts` — `CLI_TEST_FILES` and the `unit` / `unit-cli` project definitions
- `tests/main-street/vitest-cli-project-isolation.test.ts` — extend the contract with
  run-time selection and full file-coverage assertions
- `tests/tooling/` (new file, optional) — zero-file / coverage guard if not folded into the
  existing contract test
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — deterministic invocation, guard, and symptom documentation
- `scripts/` (only if a guard needs orchestration outside the Vitest suite)
- `core/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`, `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — engine
  repo; read-only here — any change is raised as a separate item in `../ContextHub`
  (producer instruction, 2026-10-23)

## Verification commands

```bash
# full suite (always via the test skill; never ad-hoc)
/skill:test

# change-scope run of only the CLI project (agent-initiated runs go through /skill:test)
npx vitest run --project unit-cli          # all five CLI files must be listed

# proof that a cached full run covered the CLI project
grep -c '|unit-cli|' .worklog/cache/<hash>/stdout.txt   # must be >= 5

# arithmetic check: non-browser test files vs reported file count
find tests -name '*.test.ts' | grep -v browser | wc -l

# wall-clock before/after: compare the `Duration` line of the cached full-suite runs
grep -h '^ *Duration' .worklog/cache/<before>/stdout.txt .worklog/cache/<after>/stdout.txt
```

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** the skip may not reproduce on demand, making "verify with a green run" weak
  evidence. Mitigation: the static coverage guard (AC3) and loud zero-file failure (AC2)
  do not depend on reproducing the quirk.
- **Risk:** two Vitest invocations add one extra collect/setup phase (~15–20 s) to a
  ~180–190 s suite. Accepted.
- **Risk:** the chosen route (fix the quirk) gives no structural guarantee, so the guard
  tests (AC3/AC4) are the real safety net; they must land even if the quirk is fixed.
- **Risk:** scope creep into diagnosing an upstream Vitest bug. Record any upstream defect
  as a separate item (`../ContextHub` per producer instruction) rather than expanding this fix.
- **Risk:** the fix silently increases suite wall-clock. Measure the full-suite duration
  before and after and record both in the item; report any increase to the producer.
- **Risk:** a re-scaffold of `vite.config.ts` drops the local `unit-cli` project. Mitigation:
  keep the documented surgical-sync note; the contract test fails loudly if it happens.
- **Assumption:** "green" means every non-browser test file ran; the 375-vs-380 arithmetic
  in the cached runs is accepted as proof of the skip.
- **Assumption:** the retry runner forwards `--project` flags correctly — verified from its
  own `[vitest-runner] ... args=` diagnostic.
- **Assumption:** the five `CLI_TEST_FILES` are the correct set (pinned by the existing
  contract test); this item does not re-scope which files are contention-prone.

---

**Headline:** `npm test` intermittently runs only the `unit` project, silently skipping the
serialized `unit-cli` project (five CLI files, including the Playwright storyline-graph SVG
guard) while still reporting green; the fix must make full-suite coverage deterministic and
make an empty configured project fail loudly.

# Add shared load-tolerant `waitForCondition` helper to `core/tests/helpers/`

Parent: MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ — make `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` waits load-tolerant.

## Goal

Give every game repo one shared browser-test poll helper whose timeout budget is
derived from the **production cap it races** rather than guessed, so a
CPU-starved host cannot make a green scene look like a red test.

## Scope (in)

1. New `core/tests/helpers/waitForCondition.ts` (sibling to `waitForScene.ts`),
   carrying the existing 49 per-file copies' behaviour **plus** a documented
   budget model:

   ```ts
   resolveWaitBudget({ capMs, starvationFactor = 1.5, floorMs = 5_000 })
     // budget = max(round(capMs * starvationFactor), capMs + floorMs)
     // throws when the result is not strictly greater than capMs
   waitForCondition(predicate, { capMs, starvationFactor?, floorMs?, intervalMs?, label? })
   ```

   - `capMs` is the **nominal** production cap (e.g. the 16 000 ms income-collection
     deferral, or `DRAG_TRANSFER_DURATION_MAX_MS`).
   - `starvationFactor` widens the nominal cap for rAF starvation (default 1.5).
   - `floorMs` guarantees a fixed scheduling margin even for tiny caps (default 5 000).
   - The invariant `budget > capMs` is enforced in code, so a caller can never
     configure a poll shorter than the cap it documents as racing.
   - Timeout message keeps the existing shape
     (`Timed out waiting for <label> after <budget>ms (cap <capMs>ms)`) so
     existing triage signatures stay greppable.
   - Raw `timeoutMs` remains accepted for callers that do not race a production
     cap (backwards-compatible with the copied implementations).

2. New `core/tests/helpers/waitForCondition.test.ts` — **written first (TDD)**:
   derivation for nominal/starvationFactor/floor, invariant throw, budget strictly
   greater than cap, predicate polling, timeout error content, `intervalMs`
   honouring.

## Scope (out)

- Migrating the 49 existing `waitForCondition` copies (explicit non-goal of the
  parent item; record as a discovered `discovered-from` item if a follow-up is
  desired).
- Any production pacing change.

## Key Files

- `core/tests/helpers/waitForCondition.ts` (new)
- `core/tests/helpers/waitForCondition.test.ts` (new)
- `configs/engine-pin.json` (pin bump)
- submodule pointer `core`

## Cross-repo workflow (core is a submodule — precedent MS-0MVKNRV6T0019KHJ)

`./core` is the `Tableau-Card-Engine` submodule, currently detached at the pinned
SHA in `configs/engine-pin.json`. Deliver this child as:

1. Implement + test in the game worktree's `core/` checkout (it is a real git
   repo there: `.git` is a gitdir file under `.git/worktrees/<wt>/modules/core`).
   If `core/` is empty in the worktree: `git submodule update --init core`.
2. In `core/`: check out `dev` (never `main`), run the affected unit suite via
   `/skill:test` in the core checkout, `npm run build` (tsc + vite) — build before
   test-commit order applies there too.
3. Commit on `dev` with the parent id, push `dev`, record the core commit hash in
   a comment on this child.
4. In the game repo: update the submodule pointer and bump `configs/engine-pin.json`
   to the new core SHA; run `npm run engine:verify`; commit the pointer + pin.
5. Record the cross-repo change on this child (core repo has no Worklog store).

**Fallback gate:** if the core push or pin bump is impossible in-session
(offline remote, core gate failure), STOP and raise an OPEN QUESTION to the
producer rather than silently relocating the helper into the game repo. If the
producer authorises relocation, the helper goes to `tests/helpers/waitForCondition.ts`
in the game repo, this child is rescoped, and the parent AC wording is amended.

## Constraints

- No Phaser import; the helper must run in both the browser project and the
  node `unit` project (it is pure `Date.now()` + `setTimeout` polling).
- Pending 60 s browser `testTimeout` headroom: default derivation must keep a
  single wait well inside 60 s (16 000 → 24 000, 1 500 → 7 500).
- Core writes follow the engine-sync workflow (`npm run engine:sync` /
  `engine:verify`); never `npm install` inside `./core` (root dependencies serve
  the engine — see `docs/dev/testing.md`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `core/tests/helpers/waitForCondition.ts` exists, exports
      `resolveWaitBudget` and `waitForCondition`, and documents the
      `nominal cap + starvation margin` model in its module docblock.
- [ ] `resolveWaitBudget` returns `max(round(capMs * starvationFactor), capMs + floorMs)`
      for the default and custom factors/floors, and throws when the derived
      budget is not strictly greater than `capMs`.
- [ ] `waitForCondition` polls at `intervalMs`, resolves on the first truthy
      predicate, and rejects with a message containing the label and the derived
      budget.
- [ ] `core/tests/helpers/waitForCondition.test.ts` covers derivation,
      the invariant throw, successful polling, and timeout (unit project, cheap).
- [ ] The affected core unit suite passes via `/skill:test` and the core build
      passes; core `dev` branch is pushed and the hash recorded on this child.
- [ ] The game repo's submodule pointer and `configs/engine-pin.json` are bumped
      to the new core SHA in the same delivery, and `npm run engine:verify` passes.
- [ ] No production pacing constant is changed.
- [ ] A shared, load-tolerant `waitForCondition` helper is added under
      `core/tests/helpers/` (sibling to `waitForScene.ts`) — the module
      docblock documents the `nominal cap + starvation margin` model.
- [ ] At least one unit test covers the new helper's budget derivation
      (`capMs` nominal, `starvationFactor`, `floorMs`), so the guard test
      above is part of the suite.

## Goal


   Assertions:
   - `resolveWaitBudget({ capMs: INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS }) > INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`;
   - `resolveWaitBudget({ capMs: DRAG_TRANSFER_DURATION_MAX_MS }) > DRAG_TRANSFER_DURATION_MAX_MS`;
   - each derived budget plus the documented boot allowance (the 20 000 ms
     `waitForScene` default) stays within the 60 000 ms browser `testTimeout`,
     so the wait always fails with its own label rather than the hook timeout;
   - the production caps are the values the tests document (16 000 /
     1 500) *only* as an assertion input derived from the imports — never as a
     restated budget literal.
2. Comment block in the guard explaining the model (`nominal cap + starvation
   margin`), why it exists (rAF starvation under host CPU contention; the retry
   runner does not retry `waitForCondition` timeouts — one spike fails the gate),
   and links to the precedent waits (`incident-reveal.browser.test.ts`
   `4_000 + 16_000`, `income-collection.browser.test.ts` `PHASED_SHOW_MS + 16000`).

## Scope (out)

- Editing `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` (the adoption child does that and
  extends this guard with its source scan).
- Deriving every other wait in the browser suite (explicit parent non-goal).
- Introducing a separate budget-constants module: the shared helper's `capMs`
  API **is** the derivation surface, so there is no second list to keep in sync.

## Key Files

- `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts` (new)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the shared helper (`core/tests/helpers/waitForCondition.ts`).
- Blocked by the exported `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` constant.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts` imports both production caps and
      the helper's `resolveWaitBudget`; it restates no budget literal.
- [x] It fails if a derived budget is not strictly greater than its production
      cap (verified by temporarily raising a cap in a scratch run — not committed).
- [x] It asserts the derived budget plus the documented boot allowance stays
      within the 60 000 ms browser `testTimeout`.
- [x] It lives in the node `unit` project (`.test.ts`, not `.browser.test.ts`) and
      runs in well under a second.
- [x] `/skill:test --type unit` (changed scope) passes.
- [x] A regression guard fails the build if any browser-test wait budget is
      smaller than the production cap it is documented as racing — the guard
      imports the cap constants rather than restating literals.

# Adopt derived wait budgets in MainStreetScene browser test

Parent: MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ — make `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` waits load-tolerant.

## Goal

Remove the two load-sensitive literals from the browser test and consume the
shared, cap-derived helper — so the Enter-to-end-turn and buy-to-hand waits can
never again be shorter than the production caps they race.

## Scope

1. In `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts`:

   - import `waitForCondition` from `@core-tests/helpers/waitForCondition`, plus
     `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` (`src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorTiming`) and
     `DRAG_TRANSFER_DURATION_MAX_MS` (`src/scenes/MainStreetConstants`);
   - `allows pressing Enter to end the turn when legal`:
     `waitForCondition(() => scene.state.turn > beforeTurn, { capMs: INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS, intervalMs: 100, label: 'turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation' })`
     — replaces `{ timeoutMs: 15_000, ... }`;
   - `only materializes purchased cards at destination after transfer animation completes`:
     `{ capMs: DRAG_TRANSFER_DURATION_MAX_MS, label: 'business bought to hand' }`;
   - the sibling `first business bought to hand` wait (same 6 000 ms, same
     transfer cap) uses `capMs: DRAG_TRANSFER_DURATION_MAX_MS` too;
   - the `hand card selected for placement` wait has no production cap to race
     (UI transition) — leave its budget, but keep it out of the guard's scope.
2. The file keeps its local `waitForCondition` for every other wait (explicit
   non-goal: no wholesale migration of the 49 copies). Mark the local copy
   `@deprecated` in a comment pointing at the shared helper.
3. Extend `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts` with a source scan of
   `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts`: for each documented label, the surrounding
   wait call must pass `capMs: INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` /

   literal — so `timeoutMs: 15_000` / `timeoutMs: 6000` cannot be reintroduced
   for those waits.
4. Update the in-test comments to explain the derivation (replace "allow the
   engine to process" with the cap + starvation-margin rationale).

      `capMs: INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` to the shared helper; no `15_000` /

# Document the load-tolerant browser wait budget model

Parent: MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ — make `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` waits load-tolerant.

## Goal

Make the new budgeting rule discoverable so future browser tests derive their
waits instead of guessing, and so the next 15 000-vs-16 000 mismatch is caught in
review rather than in a red gate.

## Scope

1. `docs/dev/testing.md` — new subsection under the browser project guidance
   ("Load-tolerant wait budgets"), covering:
   - the problem: browser tests race Phaser `requestAnimationFrame` tweens and
     bounded scene deferrals; under host CPU contention rAF starves and nominal
     durations stretch;
   - the rule: **never hard-code a wait for an animation-gated outcome** — pass
     `capMs` (the production cap) to the shared helper, which derives
     `budget = max(capMs * starvationFactor, capMs + floorMs)`;
   - the invariant: the derived budget is strictly greater than the cap, enforced
     by `resolveWaitBudget` and by `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts`;
   - the 60 000 ms `testTimeout` headroom rule (budget + boot allowance);
   - why "accept the flake" is not an option here: the retry runner
     (`core/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`) retries only the three transient
     contention signatures, not a `waitForCondition` timeout.
2. Code comments: the helper's module docblock (cross-check it matches the docs),
   `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`'s docblock, and the two adopted waits in
   `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts`.
3. `docs/dev/testing.md` soak evidence section: how to run the soak
   (`/skill:test --type soak`, or the script it wraps) and how to read its
   summary, so a future flake has a reproduction path.
4. Check for other documentation that states the old fixed budgets (grep `15_000`,
   `15000`, `6_000`, `waitForCondition`) and update the game-facing pacing notes
   (`docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`) only if they assert test-budget numbers —
   do **not** change production pacing documentation.

# Prove browser-wait reliability: 20-run soak plus under-load run

Parent: MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ — make `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` waits load-tolerant.

## Goal

Turn "20 consecutive local runs pass, including at least one under imposed CPU
load" from an anecdote into a repeatable, policy-compliant soak with recorded
evidence — so the parent AC is proven, not assumed.

## Scope

1. `scripts/soak-browser-waits.sh` (game repo `scripts/`) — soak harness:
   - loops `--runs N` (default 20) invoking the project's canonical browser
     runner, `npx tsx core/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts --project browser
     tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts`, so the retry/hang
     semantics match the real gate;
   - `--load` mode: spins up `$(nproc)` CPU burners for the duration of the run,
     records `loadavg` before/during/after, and tears them down on exit (trap);
   - aborts on the first failure (fail-fast, prints the failing run's output);
   - per-run wall time, pass/fail and peak load average in a markdown summary
     written to `results/soak-browser-waits-<timestamp>.md`; exit non-zero if any
     run fails.
2. `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` — add a project-local `soak` type
   whose command is `bash scripts/soak-browser-waits.sh --runs 20`, so the soak is
   an agent-initiated run that goes **through the test skill**
   (`/skill:test --type soak`) per the test-execution policy, instead of an ad-hoc
   loop of `npx vitest`. This is the documented extension mechanism
   (`docs/dev/skill-extensions.md`); keep the edit to that single file and record
   it as an intentional, in-scope config addition (do not otherwise touch `.pi/`).
3. Execute the soak: one quiet-host run of 20 consecutive passes, then at least
   one `--load` run. Run it as a background job per the background-job etiquette
   (launch → prepare docs/review → single completion-aware wait via
   `wait_for_job.py`, no fixed `sleep` polling).
4. Comment the evidence on this child and on the parent: run count, load
   averages, per-run durations, summary-file path, and any anomaly.

## Scope (out)

- Improving the retry runner's transient classification (separate concern; record
  as `discovered-from` if the soak reveals a genuine transient signature gap).
- Soaking any other browser file.

## Key Files

- `scripts/soak-browser-waits.sh` (new)
- `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` (new `soak` type)
- `results/soak-browser-waits-*.md` (generated; confirm `results/` is gitignored —
  if it is not, write summaries to an already-ignored path instead)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the adoption child.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `scripts/soak-browser-waits.sh --runs 20` exits 0 after 20 consecutive
      passes of `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts`, and exits
      non-zero on the first failing run.
- [x] `--load` mode imposes CPU load (≥ `nproc` burners, load average recorded),
      is cleaned up via `trap`, and at least one full under-load pass is recorded.
- [x] The soak is runnable through `/skill:test --type soak` (project-local test
      type), not by an ad-hoc `npx vitest` loop.
- [x] Evidence comment on this child and on the parent states runs, passes,
      load averages, wall times, and the summary path.
- [x] No flake was accepted: any failing run is triaged before the child closes.
- [x] Reliability proven, not assumed: at least 20 consecutive local runs of
      `npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts`
      pass (through the project soak type), including at least one run under
      imposed CPU load.
- [x] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes:
      `/skill:test` (`--type full`) is green at the end of the chain and the
      evidence is recorded on the parent.
